children.translated_text: <s>Alaṅkārasarvasvam</s> (The Compendium of All Ornaments)
Having bowed to the supreme <s>Vāc</s> (Speech), the Goddess of threefold form,
the purport of the teacher's aphorisms on ornaments is stated by way of exposition. [RuAss 0]
Introduction (<s>Bhūmikā</s>)

children.text:
iha hi tāvad bhāmahodbhaṭaprabhṛtayaścirantanālaṅkārakārāḥ pratīyamānamarthe vācyopaskārakatayālaṅkārapakṣanikṣitpaṃ manyante /
tathāhi-paryāyoktāprastutapraśaṃsāsamāsoktyākṣepavyājastutyupameyopamānanvayādau vastumātraṃ gamyamānaṃ vācyopaskārakatvena 'svasiddhaye parākṣepaḥparārthe svasamarpaṇam' iti yathāyogaṃ dvividhayā bhaṅgyā pratipāditaṃ taiḥ /
rudraṭenāpi bhāvālaṅkāro dvidhoktaḥ /
rūpakadīpakāpahnutitulyayogitādāvupamādyalaṅkāro vācyopaskārakatvenoktaḥ /
utprekṣā tu svayameva pratīyamānā kathitā /
rasavatpreyaḥprabhṛtau tu rasabhāvādirvācyaśobhāhetutvenoktaḥ /

children.translated_text: Thus, the suggested meaning in all its three forms was declared solely as ornament. [RuAss Bhū.1]

Here, first, the ancient authors on ornaments such as <s>Bhāmaha</s>, <s>Udbhaṭa</s>, and others consider the suggested meaning (<s>pratīyamāna</s>) to be placed within the category of ornament (<s>alaṅkāra</s>) as an embellisher of the expressed (<s>vācya</s>). Thus, in <s>paryāyoktā</s> (indirect expression), <s>prastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the present through the absent), <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression), <s>ākṣepa</s> (objection), <s>vyājastuti</s> (praise through censure), <s>upameyopamā</s> (comparison of the compared), <s>anvaya</s> (sequence), etc., the mere thing (<s>vastu</s>) that is understood was presented by them as an embellisher of the expressed through two types of technique as appropriate: 'the implication of another for one's own establishment' and 'the offering of oneself for another's purpose.' By <s>Rudraṭa</s> too, <s>bhāvālaṅkāra</s> (ornament of emotion) was described as twofold. In <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination), <s>apahnuti</s> (denial), <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal application), etc., the ornament of simile etc. was stated as embellishing the expressed. <s>Utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), however, was described as itself being suggested. But in <s>rasavat</s> (having <s>rasa</s>), <s>preyaḥ</s> (affection), etc., <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, etc. were stated as causes of the beauty of the expressed.

children.text:
vāmanena tu sādṛśyanibandhanāyā lakṣaṇāya vakroktyalaṅkāratvaṃ bruvatā kaściddhvanibhedo 'laṅkāratayaivoktaḥ /
kevalaṃ guṇaviśiṣṭapadaracanātmikā rītiḥ kāvyātmakatvenoktā /
udbhaṭādibhistu guṇālaṅkārāṇāṃ prāyaśaḥ sāmyameva sūcitam /
viṣayamātreṇa bhedapratipādanāt /
saṃghaṭanādharmatvena ceṣṭeḥ /
tadevamalaṅkārā eva kāvye pradhānamiti prācyānāṃ matam / [RuAss_Bhū.2]
children.translated_text: Thus, the view of the ancients is that ornaments alone are primary in poetry. [RuAss Bhū.2]

But by <s>Vāmana</s>, who declared <s>vakrokti</s> (oblique expression) to be an ornament — being based on figurative usage (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) grounded in similarity — a certain variety of <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) was stated only as an ornament. Only <s>rīti</s> (style), which consists of composition of words distinguished by <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), was declared as the essence of poetry. But by <s>Udbhaṭa</s> and others, the near-identity of <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) and <s>alaṅkāras</s> (ornaments) was generally indicated, since difference was presented only in terms of subject matter, and because this [quality] was desired as a property of composition.

children.text:
vakroktijīvitakāraḥ punarvaidagdhyabhaṅgībhaṇitisvabhāvāṃ bahuvidhāṃ vakroktimevaprādhānyātkāvyajīvitamuktavān /
vyāpārasya prādhānyaṃ ca [kāvyasya] pratipede /
abhidhānaprakāraviśeṣā eva cālaṅkārāḥ /
satyapi tribhede pratīyamāne vyāpārarūpā bhaṇitireva kavisaṃrambhagocaraḥ /
upacāravakratādibhiḥ samasto dhvaniprapañcaḥ svīkṛtaḥ /
kevalamuktivaicitryajīvitaṃ kāvyaṃ, na vyaṅgyārthajīvitamiti tadīyaṃ darśanaṃ vyavasthitam / [RuAss_Bhū.3]
children.translated_text: Only this much is established as his view: poetry has its life in the variety of expression, not in the suggested meaning. [RuAss Bhū.3]

The author of the <s>Vakroktijīvita</s> (<s>Kuntaka</s>), on the other hand, declared the manifold <s>vakrokti</s> (oblique expression), whose nature is the utterance of the mode of wit (<s>vaidagdhya</s>), to be the life of poetry due to its primacy. And he accepted the primacy of the operation (<s>vyāpāra</s>) in poetry. And ornaments are simply particular modes of expression (<s>abhidhānaprakāraviśeṣa</s>). Even though the suggested meaning is threefold, only the utterance in the form of operation is the domain of the poet's effort. Through figurative obliquity (<s>upacāravakratā</s>) and other means, the entire elaboration of <s>dhvani</s> was encompassed.

children.text: bhaṭṭanāyakena tu vyaṅgyavyāpārasya prauḍhoktyābhyupagatasya kāvyaṃśatvaṃ bruvatā nyagbhāvitaśabdārthasvarūpasya vyāpārasyaiva prādhānyamuktam /

children.translated_text: Therein too, the operation called <s>bhoga</s> (enjoyment), synonymous with the relishing of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), transcending the two operations of <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation) and <s>bhāvakatva</s> (actualization), was accepted as primary, being the resting-place. [RuAss Bhū.4]

But by <s>Bhaṭṭanāyaka</s>, who — while accepting through mature assertion the status of the suggestive operation (<s>vyaṅgyavyāpāra</s>) as a component of poetry — subordinated the nature of word and meaning, the primacy of the operation itself was declared.

children.text:
dhvanikāraḥ punarabhidhātātparyalakṣaṇākhyavyāpāratrayottīrṇasya dhvananadyotanādiśabdābhidheyasya vyañjanavyāpārasyāvaśyābhyupagamyatvād vyāpārasya ca vākyārthatvābhāvād vākyārthasyaiva ca vyāṅgyarūpasya guṇālaṅkāropaskartavyatvena prādhānyād viśrāntidhāmatvādātmatvaṃ sidhdāntitavān /
vyāpārasya viṣayamukhena svaruṇpratilambhāt tatprādhānyena prādhānyāt svarūpeṇa vicāryatvābhāvād viṣayasyaiva samagrabharasahiṣṇutvam /
tasmād viṣaya eva vyaṅgyanāmā jīvitatvena vaktavyaḥ,yasya guṇālaṅkārakṛtacārutvaparigrahasābhrājyam /
rasādayastu jīvitabhūtā nālaṅkāratvenavācyāḥ /
alaṅkārāṇāmupaskārakatvād,rasādīnāṃ ca prādhānyenopaskāryatvāt /
tasmād vyaṅgya eva vākyārthībhūtaḥ kāvyajīvitamityeṣa eva pakṣo vākyārthavidāṃ sahṛdayānāmāvarjakaḥ /

children.translated_text: Because the operation of suggestion (<s>vyañjanā</s>) is not denied by anyone, and because no alternative position is tenable on its basis. [RuAss Bhū.5]

The <s>Dhvanikāra</s> (author of the <s>Dhvanyāloka</s>, <s>Ānandavardhana</s>), however, established as the soul [of poetry] the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) — which is designated by terms such as '<s>dhvanana</s>' (resonance) and '<s>dyotana</s>' (illumination), and which transcends the three operations called <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation), <s>tātparya</s> (purport), and <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (figurative usage) — since the operation of suggestion (<s>vyañjana</s>) must necessarily be accepted, and since the operation does not constitute sentence-meaning, and since the sentence-meaning itself in the form of the suggested, being primary as that which is to be embellished by <s>guṇas</s> and <s>alaṅkāras</s>, is the resting-place of aesthetic repose, and hence the soul [of poetry]. Since the operation attains its own nature only through its object, and since the operation's primacy entails the object's primacy, and since the operation has no independent status for examination apart from [its object], only the object bears the entire weight. Therefore, the object alone, called the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>), is to be declared the life [of poetry] — that which shines with the beauty created by <s>guṇas</s> and <s>alaṅkāras</s>. But <s>rasa</s> and the rest, being the life [of poetry], are not to be called ornaments, since ornaments are embellishers, while <s>rasa</s> etc. are primarily what is to be embellished. Therefore, the suggested meaning alone, having become the sentence-meaning, is the life of poetry — this very position alone captivates the connoisseurs (<s>sahṛdayas</s>) who understand sentence-meaning.

children.text: yattu vyaktivivekakāro vācyasya pratīyamānaṃ prati liṅgatayā vyañjanasyānumānāntarbhāvamākhyat tad vācyasya pratīyamānena saha tādāpmyatadutpattyabhāvādavicāritābhidhānam /

children.translated_text: Since this is to be examined by those of sharp intelligence and is extremely profound, it is not elaborated here. [RuAss Bhū.6]

But the author of the <s>Vyaktiviveka</s> (<s>Mahimabhaṭṭa</s>), who declared the subsumption of suggestion under inference (<s>anumāna</s>) because the expressed serves as an indicatory sign (<s>liṅga</s>) for the suggested — that [claim] is carelessly stated, since there is no identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) or causal relation (<s>tadutpatti</s>) between the expressed and the suggested.

children.text:
astiṃ tāvad vyaṅgyaniṣṭo vyañjanavyāpāraḥ /
tatra vyaṅgyasya prādhānyāprādhānyābhyāṃ dhvaniguṇībhūtavyaṅgyākhyau dvau kāvyabhedau /
vyaṅgyasyāsphuṭatve 'laṅkārattvena citrākhyaḥ kāvyabhedastṛtīyaḥ /
tatrottamo dhvaniḥ /
tasya lakṣaṇābhidhāmūlatvenāvivakṣitavācyavivakṣitānyaparavācyavivakṣitānyaparavācyākhyau dvau bhedau /
ādyo 'pyarthāntarasaṃkramasaṃsalakṣyakramitavācyātyāntatiraskṛtavācyatvena dvividhaḥ /
dvitīyo 'pyasaṃlakṣyakramasaṃlakṣyakramavyaṅgyatayā dvividhaḥ /
lakṣaṇāmūlaḥ śabdaśaktimūlo vastudhvaniḥ,asaṃlakṣyakramavyaṅgyaḥ arthaśaktimūlo rasādidhvaniḥ /
saṃlakṣyakramavyaṅgyaḥ śabdārthobhayaśaktimūlo vastudhvaniralaṅkāradhvaniśceti /
tatra rasādidhvaniralaṅkāramañjaryāṃ darśitaḥ, kāvyasya śṛṅgārapradhānatvāt /
śiṣṭastu yathāvasaraṃ tatraiva vibhaktaḥ /

children.translated_text: The subordinated suggested meaning (<s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>) was shown as appropriate in <s>samāsokti</s> etc., through the distinctions of being subsidiary to the expressed etc. [RuAss Bhū.7]

Now, there does exist the operation of suggestion based on the suggested meaning. Therein, by the primacy or non-primacy of the suggested, there are two types of poetry called <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) and <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion). When the suggested is indistinct, being in the nature of ornament, there is a third type of poetry called <s>citra</s> (pictorial). Among these, <s>dhvani</s> is the highest. It has two divisions called <s>avivakṣitavācya</s> (unintended expressed meaning) and <s>vivakṣitānyaparavācya</s> (intended other-primary expressed meaning), based on whether it is rooted in <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (figurative usage) or <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation). The first is again twofold: <s>arthāntarasaṃkramita</s> (transferred to another meaning) and <s>atyantātiraskṛtavācya</s> (completely concealed expressed meaning). The second is also twofold: <s>asaṃlakṣyakrama</s> (imperceptible sequence) and <s>saṃlakṣyakrama</s> (perceptible sequence) suggestion. That rooted in <s>lakṣaṇā</s> and word-power is <s>vastudhvani</s> (suggestion of fact); <s>asaṃlakṣyakrama</s> suggestion rooted in meaning-power is <s>rasādidhvani</s> (suggestion of <s>rasa</s> etc.); <s>saṃlakṣyakrama</s> suggestion rooted in word-power, meaning-power, or both is <s>vastudhvani</s> (suggestion of fact) and <s>alaṅkāradhvani</s> (suggestion of ornament). Among these, <s>rasādidhvani</s> was shown in the <s>Alaṅkāramañjarī</s>, since poetry is primarily erotic (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>). The rest was distributed therein as the occasion arose.
<s>Sūtra</s> 1:

children.text:
citraṃ tu śabdārthāṃlakārasvabhāvatayā bahutaraprabhedam /
tathā hi-
children.translated_text: <s>Citra</s> (pictorial poetry), however, being of the nature of ornaments of word and meaning, has very many varieties. Thus—

children.text: ihārthapaunaruktyaṃ śabdapaunaruktyaṃ śabdārthapaunaruktyaṃ ceti trayaḥ paunaruktyaprakārāḥ || 1 ||
children.translated_text: Here, there are three types of repetition (<s>paunaruktya</s>): repetition of meaning (<s>arthapaunaruktya</s>), repetition of word (<s>śabdapaunaruktya</s>), and repetition of word-and-meaning (<s>śabdārthapaunaruktya</s>). [RuAss 1]

children.text:
ādau paunaruktyaprakāraravacanaṃ vakṣyamāṇālaṅkārāṇāṃ kakṣāvibhāgaghaṭanārtham /
arthāpekṣayā śabdasya pratītāvantaraṅgatve 'pi prathamamarthatadharmanirdeśaścirantanaprasiddhyā punaruktakavadābhāsasya pūrvaṃ lakṣaṇārthaḥ /
ihaśabdaḥ pratthāne /
itiśabdaḥ prakāre, triśabdādeva saṃkhyāparisamātpisiddheḥ /
children.translated_text: The statement of the types of repetition at the outset is for the purpose of establishing the division of ranks among the ornaments to be discussed. Even though word is more internal than meaning with respect to cognition, meaning and its properties are presented first, due to the long-standing convention, for the purpose of defining what appears to be repetition (<s>punaruktavadābhāsa</s>). The word 'here' (<s>iha</s>) indicates commencement. The word 'thus' (<s>iti</s>) indicates the types, since the exact number is already established from the word 'three' (<s>tri</s>) alone.
<s>Sūtra</s> 2:
Among these, well-established (<s>praruḍha</s>) repetition of meaning is a fault (<s>doṣa</s>). [RuAss 2]

children.text:
praruḍhāpraruḍhatvena dvaividhyam /
prathamaṃ heyavacanamupādeye viśrāntyartham /
tatreti trayanirdhāraṇe /
yathāvabhāsanaviśrāntiḥ prarohaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is a twofold division into well-established and non-well-established (<s>praruḍha</s> and <s>apraruḍha</s>). The first [statement that it is a fault] is for the purpose of establishing repose in what is to be accepted. 'Among these' (<s>tatra</s>) serves to distinguish the three. The manifestation as it naturally appears is called 'establishment' (<s>praroha</s>).
<s>Sūtra</s> 3:
Repeated manifestation at the beginning is 'apparent repetition' (<s>punaruktavadābhāsa</s>). [RuAss 3]

children.text:
āmukhagrahaṇaṃ paryavasāne 'nyathātvapratipattyartham /
lakṣyanirdeśe nāpuṃsakaḥ saṃskāro laukikālaṅkāravaidharyeṇa kāvyālaṅkāraṇāmalaṅkāryaṃpāratantryadhvananārthaḥ /
arthapaunaruktyādevārthīśritatvādarthālaṅkāratvaṃ jñeyam /
prabhedāstu vistarabhayānnocyante /
udāharaṇaṃ madīye śrīkaṇṭhastave yathā-
children.translated_text: The use of the word 'beginning' (<s>āmukha</s>) is for the purpose of understanding the difference at the conclusion. In the citation of examples, the neuter grammatical form indicates, by contrast with worldly ornament, that poetic ornaments are dependent on what is to be ornamented — thus suggesting [their] dependent nature. Since it depends on repetition of meaning, its status as an ornament of meaning should be understood. The sub-varieties are not stated for fear of prolixity. An example from my own hymn to Śrī <s>Kaṇṭha</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), as follows—
"Whose body-bracelet is the king of serpents with abundant snakes,
whose sport is of the mountain-born (<s>Pārvatī</s>) and <s>Nandī</s>, who destroyed the pride of <s>Kandara</s> (<s>Kāmadeva</s>),
whose mark is the bull, chief among bulls, whose eye is the peacock-fire (<s>Śiva</s>'s third eye),
I praise that <s>Īśvara</s>, companion of <s>Pārvatī</s>, together with <s>Sarvamaṅgalā</s> (the all-auspicious one)."
"Terrible, born from wood, the supreme one whose glory is of ashes,
red, of crimson flame, exceedingly fierce — may <s>Pāvaka</s> (Fire), the crested one, protect you!"
"The serpent-ringed one, clearly radiant with the cool-rayed moon's white beams,
may <s>Śiva</s>, who steals the heart, always protect the worlds from destruction."
<s>Sūtra</s> 4:
Repetition of word (<s>śabdapaunaruktya</s>) is [of two kinds]: repetition of consonants alone, and repetition of the combination of vowels and consonants. [RuAss 4]

children.text: alaṃkāraprastāve kevalaṃ svarapaunaruktyamacārutvānna gaṇyate iti dvaividhyameva /
children.translated_text: In the context of ornaments, repetition of vowels alone is not counted because it lacks beauty — thus there is only a twofold division.
<s>Sūtra</s> 5:
When there is a restriction on the number, first [considering] the combination of consonants, it is <s>chekānuprāsa</s> (witty alliteration). [RuAss 5]

children.text:
dvayorvyañjanasamudāyayoḥ parasparamanaikadhā sādṛśyaṃ saṃkhyāniyamaḥ /
pūrvaṃ vyañjamasamudāyāśritaṃ yathā-
children.translated_text: The restricted numerical similarity between two groups of consonants, occurring in more than one way, is 'restriction on number.' 'First' refers to that which depends on the combination of consonants. For example—

children.text: 'kiṃ nāma dardura duradhyavasāya sāyaṃ kāyaṃ nipīḍya ninadaṃ kuruṣe ruṣeva /
children.translated_text: "Why indeed, O frog, do you make such noise in the evening with such difficult resolve, pressing your body as if in anger?

children.text: etāni kelirasitāni sitacchadānāmākarṇya kārṇamadhurāṇi na lajjito 'si' //
children.translated_text: Are you not ashamed, having heard these playful laughter-like sounds of the white-winged ones (swans), sweet to the ear?"

children.text:
atra sāyaṃśabdenāsyālaṅkārasya yakāramātrasādṛśyāpekṣayā vṛttyanuprāsena sahaikābhidhānalakṣaṇaḥ saṃkaraḥ /
chekā vidagdhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, with the word '<s>sāyam</s>' (evening), since this ornament requires only the similarity of the ya-consonant, there is a conflation (<s>saṃkara</s>) with <s>vṛttyanuprāsa</s> (flowing alliteration), characterized by a single statement. '<s>Chekā</s>' means 'the witty ones' (<s>vidagdhāḥ</s>).
<s>Sūtra</s> 6:
Otherwise, it is <s>vṛttyanuprāsa</s> (flowing alliteration). [RuAss 6]

children.text:
kevalavyañjanamātrasādṛśyamekadhā samudāyasādṛśyaṃ tryādīnāṃ ca parasparasādṛśyamānyathābhāvaḥ /
vṛttistu rasaviṣayo vyāpāraḥ /
tadvatī punarvarṇaracanehavṛttiḥ /
sa ca paruṣakomalamadhyamavarṇārabdhatvāttridhā /
tadupalakṣito 'yamanuprāsaḥ /
yathā-
children.translated_text: Resemblance in mere consonants alone is one type; resemblance in combinations [of syllables] is another; and mutual resemblance of three or more [syllables] constitutes yet another variety. <s>Vṛtti</s> (style), however, is a function pertaining to <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment). [The verse] possessing that [function] is where this <s>vṛtti</s> resides in the arrangement of phonemes. And it is threefold, since it is constituted of harsh, soft, and middle phonemes. This <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) is characterized by that [vṛtti]. For example:

children.text: 'āṭopena paṭīyayasā yadapi sā vāṇī kaverāmukhe khelantī prathame tathāpi kurute no sanmanorañjanam /
children.translated_text: 'Even though the speech of a poet plays at the tip of his tongue with bombast and cleverness, it does not produce true delight for the refined mind,
unless there is a <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) that follows the stream of rich, sweet, flowing, beautiful qualities and ornamental resonance.'
Or for example:

children.text: 'sahyāḥ pannagaphūtkṛtānalaśikhā nārācapālyo 'pi vā rākendoḥ kiraṇā viṣadravamuco varṣāsu vā vāyavaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Endurable are the flame-tongues of serpent-hisses, or the showers of arrows, or the rays of the full moon, or the winds of the rainy season that release streams of poison;

children.text: na tvetāḥ saralāḥ sitāsitarucaḥ sācīkṛtāḥ sālasāḥ sākūtāḥ samadāḥ kuraṅgakadṛśāṃ mānānuvidhdā dṛśaḥ' //
children.translated_text: but not these glances of the doe-eyed women — straight yet oblique, bright and dark, languid, meaningful, intoxicated, directed by wounded pride.'
START Sūtra 7:
Repetition of vowels, consonants, or their combinations is <s>yamaka</s> (rhyme/wordplay). // RuAss 7 //

children.text:
atra kvacidbhinnārthatvaṃ kvicidabhinnārthatvaṃ kacidekasyānarthakatvamaparasya sārthakatvamiti saṃkṣepataḥ prakāratrayam /
yathā-
children.translated_text: Here there are broadly three varieties: sometimes with different meanings, sometimes with identical meanings, and sometimes one [occurrence] is meaningless while the other is meaningful. For example:
'Whoever sees those two charming eyes — in a forest she is born (vana-jāyate) /
in that person's other eyes, charm (ruci) indeed does not arise (na jāyate).'
This is [an example] with meaningfulness. Other [types] should be understood similarly.
START Sūtra 8:
"Repetition of word and meaning that is well-established is a fault (<s>doṣa</s>)." // RuAss 8 //

children.text:
praruḍhagrahaṇaṃ vakṣyamāṇaprabhedavailakṣaṇyārtham /
yadāhuḥ-'śabdārthayoḥ punarvacanaṃ punaruktamanyatrānuvādāt' /
iti /
children.translated_text: The word 'well-established' (<s>praruḍha</s>) is [included] to distinguish [this] from the varieties to be discussed later. As they say: 'The saying again of word and meaning is repetition (<s>punarukta</s>), except in the case of restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>).'
START Sūtra 9:
'But when there is a difference in purport, it is <s>lāṭānuprāsa</s> (repetition with changed import).' // RuAss 9 //
For example:

children.text: 'tālā jaanti guṇā jālā de sahiaehiṃ gheppanti /
children.translated_text: 'Then qualities are born, when they are grasped by the sensitive (<s>sahṛdayas</s>).
Favored by the rays of the sun, the lotuses become [truly] lotuses.'
<s>Tātparya</s> (purport) means having a different referent. It is the purport alone that differs, not the essential form of word and meaning.
[Sanskrit rendering:] 'Then qualities are born, when they are grasped by the sensitive (<s>sahṛdayas</s>).
Favored by the rays of the sun, the lotuses become [truly] lotuses.'

children.text: 'brūmaḥ kiyannaya kathañcana kālamalpam atrābjapatranayane nayane nimīlya /
children.translated_text: 'We say: close for just a short while, somehow, for a moment, O girl with eyes like lotus petals, your eyes.
O young woman, taking that golden lotus quickly with excitement — know that this enemy of the gods (demon) has come, saying "I am he!"'
In such cases, even though there is no repetition of case-endings etc., because there is extensive repetition of both word and meaning, it is indeed <s>lāṭānuprāsa</s>.
'The <s>kāśa</s> grasses appear like <s>kāśa</s> grasses, and the lakes like lakes;
the submerged [beauties] captivated the hearts of young men, like submerged [beauties].'
In such cases, there is no confusion (<s>saṃkara</s>) with <s>ananvaya</s> (self-comparison), whose defining characteristic is identity of expression,
because the two have different domains — one pertaining to both word and meaning through mutual dependence, and the other pertaining to meaning alone.
'In <s>ananvaya</s>, the identity of words is incidental, arising from propriety;
but in this <s>lāṭānuprāsa</s>, it is the direct cause.'
START Sūtra 10:
Thus, in the domain of repetition, there are five <s>alaṅkāras</s> (figures of speech). // RuAss 10 //
This is explained by the statement itself (self-evident).
START Sūtra 11:
When phonemes are the cause of producing the form of a sword etc., it is <s>citra</s> (pattern poetry). // RuAss 11 //

children.text:
paunaruktakyaprastāve sthānaviśeṣaśliṣṭavarṇapaunaruktyātmakaṃ citravacanam /
yadyapi lipyakṣarāṇāṃ khaṅgādisaṃniveśaviśiṣṭatvaṃ tathāpi śrotrākāśasamavetavarṇātmakaśabdābhedena teṣāṃ loke pratītervācakaśabdālaṅkāro 'yam /
ādiprahaṇād yathāvyutpattisaṃbhavaṃ padmabandhādiparigrahaḥ /

children.translated_text: For example:
'She shines with reflected splendor, radiant in essence, robbed of glow by destruction,
her soul illumined, in auspicious speech, with divine luster — behold, the assembly!'

In the context of repetition, this is pattern-composition (<s>citra-vacana</s>), consisting of the repetition of phonemes adhering to specific positions. Although the written characters have the distinctive arrangement of a sword etc., nevertheless, since in common usage they are understood as identical with the word constituted of phonemes perceived in the space of hearing, this is an <s>alaṅkāra</s> (ornament) of the expressive word. By the word 'etc.' (<s>ādi</s>), the inclusion of lotus-pattern (<s>padma-bandha</s>) and similar [forms] is indicated, as far as their construction is possible. For example:

children.text:
eṣo 'ṣṭadalapadmabanadhaḥ /
atra digdaleṣu nirgamapraveśābhyāṃ śliṣṭākṣaratvam /
vivigdaleṣu tvanyathā /
karṇikākṣaraṃ tu śliṣṭameva /
children.translated_text: This is an eight-petaled lotus pattern (<s>aṣṭa-dala-padma-bandha</s>). Here, in the directional petals, the syllables are connected through exit and entry. In the intermediate petals, however, [they are connected] differently. The central syllable (<s>karṇikā</s>) is always connected.
START Sūtra 12:

When there is common property between the standard of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) and the subject of comparison (<s>upameya</s>), with equality of difference and non-difference, it is <s>upamā</s> (simile). // RuAss 12 //

children.text:
arthālaṅkāraprakaraṇamidam /
upamānopameyayorityapratītopamānopameyaniṣedhārtham /
sādhrmye trayaḥ prakārāḥ /
bhedaprādhānyaṃ vyatirekādivat /
abhedaprādhānyaṃ rūpakādivat /
dvayostulyatvaṃ yathāsyām /
yadāhuḥ-'yatra kiñcitsāmānyaṃ kaściñca viśeṣaḥ sa viṣayaḥ sadṛśatāyāḥ' iti /
upamaivanekaprakāravaicitryeṇānekālaṅkārabūjabhūteti prathamaṃ nirdiṣṭā /
asyāśca pūrṇālutpātvabhedāñcirantanairbahuvidhanvamuktam /
tatrāpi sādhāraṇadharmsya kvacidanurāgāmitayaikarūpyeṇa nirdeśaḥ, kvacidvastuprativastubhāvena pṛthaṅnirdeśaḥ /
pṛthaṅnirdeśe ca saṃbandhibhedamātraṃ prativastūpamāvat, bimbapratibimbabhāvo vā dṛṣṭāntavat /
krameṇodāharaṇam -
children.translated_text: This is the section on <s>arthālaṅkāra</s> (figures of meaning). [The phrase] 'of the <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s>' is [included] to exclude cases where the standard or subject of comparison is not recognized. In [the domain of] common property, there are three varieties: predominance of difference, as in <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) etc.; predominance of non-difference, as in <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) etc.; and equality of both — as in this [<s>upamā</s>]. As they say: 'Where there is some commonality and some distinction, that is the domain of resemblance.' <s>Upamā</s> (simile) itself, through the variety of its many forms, is the seed of many <s>alaṅkāras</s>, and so it is described first. And the ancients have explained its many varieties through the distinctions of full (<s>pūrṇā</s>) and partial (<s>luptā</s>). Even within those, the common property is sometimes stated in a unified manner through the resemblance of affection etc., and sometimes stated separately as a thing-and-counterpart relationship. In the separate statement, either there is mere difference of the related [terms], as in <s>prativastūpamā</s> (counterpart simile), or there is a reflection-and-original relationship, as in <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (illustrative example). Examples in order:
'Like a lamp [bright] with the act of bowing, like the three-fold path of the celestials,

children.text: saṃskāravatyeva girā manīṣī tayā sa pūtaśca vibhūṣitaśca' //
children.translated_text: like speech endowed with refinement — by her, the wise man was both purified and adorned.'
'As she goes, repeatedly turning her neck, bearing that face

children.text: digdho 'mṛtena ca viṣeṇa ca pakṣmalākṣyā gāḍhaṃ nikhāta iva me hṛdaye kaṭākṣaḥ' //
children.translated_text: resembling a hundred-petaled lotus turned upon its stalk — by the large-eyed one, her sidelong glance, smeared with both nectar and poison, is deeply planted in my heart as if driven in.'
Here, the turning and the being-turned-upon are different due to difference in the related [terms].
But from the standpoint of the common property, it is indeed a reflection-and-original relationship.
'This <s>Pāṇḍya</s> king, with a long garland placed upon his shoulders, his body anointed with <s>haricandana</s> (yellow sandalwood),
appears like the king of mountains, its peak reddened by the morning sun, with waterfalls gushing forth.'
Here, the garland and the body-paint are described as reflections of the waterfall and the morning sunlight.
START Sūtra 13:
When one and the same thing is both the standard and the subject of comparison, it is <s>ananvaya</s> (self-comparison). // RuAss 13 //

children.text:
vācyābhiprāyeṇa pūrvaṃrūpānugamaḥ /
ekasya tu viruddhadharmasaṃsargo dvitīyasavrahyacārinivṛttyarthaḥ /
ata evānanvaya iti yogo 'pyatra saṃbhravati /

children.translated_text: For example:

children.text: 'yuddhe 'rjuno 'rjuna iva prathitapratāpo bhīmo 'pi bhīma iva vairiṣu bhīmakarmā /
children.translated_text: 'In battle, <s>Arjuna</s>, famous for his valor like <s>Arjuna</s> [himself], and <s>Bhīma</s> too, of terrible deeds against foes like <s>Bhīma</s> [himself],
went with respect to the <s>Kuru</s> king who resided at <s>Nyagrodha</s>, as if to console him.'

From the standpoint of the expressed [meaning], this is a continuation of the previous form. But the association of contradictory properties in one [entity] is for the purpose of excluding any second companion [i.e., nothing else compares]. Therefore the term '<s>ananvaya</s>' (without parallel) is also appropriate here.
START Sūtra 14:
When two [things] alternately [serve as standard and subject], it is <s>upameyopamā</s> (mutual comparison). // RuAss 14 //

children.text:
tacchabdenopamānopameyatvapratyavamarśaḥ /
paryāyo yaugapadyābhāvaḥ /
ata evātra vākyabhedaḥ /
iyaṃ ca dharmasya sādhāraṇye vastuprativastunirdeśe ca dvidhā /

children.translated_text: In the first case, for example:

children.text: 'khamiva jalaṃ jalamiva khaṃ haṃsaścandra iva haṃsa iva candraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The sky is like the water, the water like the sky; the swan is like the moon, the moon like the swan;
the stars are in the form of lotuses, the lotuses in the form of stars.'

By the word 'that' (<s>tad</s>), the reference back to the [conditions of] being standard and subject of comparison is indicated. 'Alternately' means the absence of simultaneity. Therefore, here there is a separation of sentences. And this is twofold: with a common property shared [between the terms], and with a thing-and-counterpart statement.
In the second case, for example:
'The lotus-faced ones have beautiful shade, and the lotuses have faces with beautiful shade;
the ponds appear like women, and the women like ponds.'
START Sūtra 15:
The remembrance of another thing from the experience of a similar one is <s>smaraṇa</s> (reminiscence). // RuAss 15 //
The 'other thing' is indeed a similar one. Because there is no invariable concomitance, it is not inference (<s>anumāna</s>). For example:
'Seeing this child of surpassing power over gods and demons, of exactly similar form,
I remember <s>Raghunandana</s> (<s>Rāma</s>), the son of <s>Kuśika</s>, holding his bow at the destruction of the enemies of sacrifice.'
But remembrance without resemblance is not this <s>alaṅkāra</s>. For example:
'Here, on the bank of this river, having returned from the hunt, with fatigue removed by the breeze from the waves,
I remember [how I] slept in the reed-houses, with [your] head resting privately on my lap.'
And here, where the qualifications of the agent describe the state of the remembered [scene] rather than the state of the rememberer, [the example] is not fitting.

children.text:
preyolaṅkārasya tu sādṛśyavyatiriktanimittotthāpitā smṛtirviṣayaḥ /
yathā
'aho kope 'pi kāntaṃ mukham' iti /

children.translated_text: Even there, when the <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) etc. are suggested and only the bare word indicates [the sentiment], as in:
'Here, on the bank of this river...' and so forth.

children.text: 'yairdṛṣṭo 'si tadā lalāṭapatitaprāsaprahāro yudhi sphītāsṛkstrutipāṭalīkṛtapurobhāgaḥ parān pātayan /
children.translated_text: 'Those who saw you then in battle — with spear-blows falling on your forehead, the front of your body reddened by copious streams of blood, slaying enemies —

children.text: teṣāṃ duḥsahakāmadehadahanaprodbhatanetrānala- jvālālībharabhāsvare smaripāvastaṃ gataṃ kautukam' //
children.translated_text: in their eyes, the fire-flames born from the raging fire of unbearable Kāmadeva's body-burning, their curiosity has set [like the sun] in the memory of the warrior.'

For the <s>preyas alaṅkāra</s> (figure of endearment), however, the subject is remembrance evoked by a cause other than resemblance. For example, 'Ah, even in anger, the beloved's face!' and so forth.

children.text:
ityādau sadṛśavastvantarānubhave 'śakyavastvantarakaraṇātmā viśeṣālaṅkāraḥ, kāraṇasya kriyāsāmānyātmano darśine 'pi saṃbhavāt /
matāntare kāvyaliṅgametat /
tadete sādṛśyāśrayeṇa bhedābhedatulyatvenālaṅkārā nirṇītāḥ" /
children.translated_text: In such cases, when there is an experience of a similar other thing, the specific <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure) consisting of the impossibility of producing another comparable thing [is identified]; because the cause, being of the general nature of action, is possible even for one who merely sees. In another view, this is <s>kāvyaliṅga</s> (poetic reason). Thus these <s>alaṅkāras</s> based on resemblance have been determined according to the equality of difference and non-difference.
START Sūtra 16:
When non-difference predominates, with superimposition (<s>āropa</s>) where the object of superimposition is not denied, it is <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor). // RuAss 16 //

children.text:
abhedasya prādhānyādbhedasya vastutaḥ sadbhāvaḥ /
anyatrānyāvāpa āropaḥ /
tasya viṣayaviṣayyavaṣṭabdhatvādviṣayasyāpahnave 'pahnutiḥ /
anyathā tu viṣayiṇā viṣayasya rūpavataḥ karaṇādrūpakam /
sādharmye tvanugatameva /
yadāhuḥ-
'upamaiva turobhūtabhedā rūpakamiṣyate' iti āropādabhede 'dhyavasāyaḥ prakṛṣyate iti paścāttanmūlālaṅkāravibhāgaḥ /
children.translated_text: When non-difference is predominant, while difference actually exists, there is superimposition (<s>āropa</s>) of one thing upon another. When the subject (<s>viṣaya</s>) is denied—since [the superimposition] is grounded in both subject and superimposed entity—it is <s>apahṇuti</s> (concealment). Otherwise, the fashioning of the subject, which possesses form, by the superimposed entity, is <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor). In the case of shared properties, it is simply pervading. As they say: '<s>upamā</s> (simile) with obliterated distinction is considered <s>rūpaka</s>' — from superimposition, when non-difference is intensified through determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>), the classification of figures based upon that [follows] hereafter.

children.text:
idaṃ tu niravayavaṃ sāvayavaṃ paramparitamiti trividham /
ādyaṃ kevalaṃ māvārūpakañcate dvidhā /
dvitīyaṃ samastavastuviṣayamekadeśavivarti ceti dvidhaiva /
tṛtīyaṃ śliṣṭaśabdanibandhanatvena dvividhaṃ satpratyekaṃ kevalamālārūpakatvāccaturvidham /
tadevamaṣṭau rūpakabhedāḥ /
anye tū pratyekaṃ vākyoktasamāsoktādibhedāḥ saṃbhavanti te 'nyato draṣṭavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: This [<s>rūpaka</s>] is of three kinds: without parts (<s>niravayava</s>), with parts (<s>sāvayava</s>), and chain-like (<s>paramparita</s>). The first is of two kinds: simple (<s>kevala</s>) and garland-<s>rūpaka</s> (<s>mālā-rūpaka</s>). The second is of two kinds: one whose subject is the entire entity (<s>samasta-vastu-viṣaya</s>), and one that extends to only a portion (<s>ekadeśa-vivarti</s>). The third, being based on words with double meaning (<s>śliṣṭa-śabda</s>), is twofold, and each being simple and garland-<s>rūpaka</s>, is fourfold. Thus there are eight varieties of <s>rūpaka</s>. Other sub-varieties such as <s>vākyokta</s> (explicitly stated), <s>samāsokta</s> (compoundly stated), etc. are possible for each; those should be examined elsewhere.
In order, as follows—

children.text: 'dāse kṛtāgāsi bhavatyucitaḥ prabhūṇāṃ pādaprahāra iti sundari nāsmi dūye /
children.translated_text: 'The kick of masters is fitting for a servant who has committed an offense, O beautiful one, so I do not grieve;

children.text: udyatkaṭhorapulakāṅkurakaṇṭakāgrair- yatkhidyate tava padaṃ nanu sā vyathā me' //
children.translated_text: rather, my pain is that your foot is hurt by the sharp tips of the thorns of the erect, hard horripilation [on my body].'
'A new stream of nectar for the sacrificial gods, a gift for the cutting of darkness, a vine of lotus-stalks at whose sight the <s>cakravāka</s> birds on the celestial <s>Gaṅgā</s> are startled;

children.text: dvirbhāvaḥ smarakārmukasya kimapi prāṇeśvarīsāgasā- māśātanturudañcati pratipadi prāleyabhānostanuḥ' //
children.translated_text: a doubling, as it were, of the bow of the god of love, an excuse for the offenses of the beloved—the thread of hope rises on the first day of the bright fortnight: the body of the snow-rayed [moon].'
'On the broad expanse of the sky-surface as a leaf-plate, the generous portion of abundant food bright as <s>kunda</s> blossoms,
smeared with dense buffalo-milk in the form of the waves of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>—this was eaten by me, O king, in the era of <s>Kali</s>.'
'This line of the dark <s>tamāla</s> forest of the sword-flesh-creeper of your night-like [fame], O king, appears—

children.text: indutviṣo yudhi haṭhena tavārikīrtī- rānīya yatra ramate taruṇaḥ pratāpaḥ' //
children.translated_text: where your youthful prowess, having forcibly brought the fame of your enemies, bright as moonlight, in battle, delights.'
Chain-like (<s>paramparita</s>)—

children.text: 'kiṃ padmamya ruciṃ na hanti nayanānandaṃ vidhatte na vā vṛddhiṃ vā jhaṣaketanasya kurute nālokamātreṇa kim /
children.translated_text: 'Does this not destroy the beauty of the lotus? Does it not bestow delight to the eyes? Does it not cause the growth of the flower-bannered god of love by mere sight?

children.text: vaktrendau tava satyayaṃ yadaparaḥ śītāṃśurabhyudgato darpaḥ syādamṛtena cidiha tadapyastyeva bimbādhare' //
children.translated_text: In the moon of your face, truly, another cool-rayed [moon] has risen; if you say the pride comes from nectar, that too indeed exists in your <s>bimba</s>-fruit lip.'
Here 'kṣitibhṛt' (mountain/king) is a word with double meaning (<s>śliṣṭa-pada</s>).
Here, the metaphorical identification of the nectar of the lip—caused by the metaphor of the face as a moon—with ambrosia is a <s>rūpaka</s> based on a word with double meaning (<s>śliṣṭa-śabda</s>).

'O swan of the lake of scholars' minds, O fire of acceptance in battle—red and blue [like blood and steel]—with the enemy who contracts in fear from the lotus [of your splendor]; O <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (universal fire) of encountering the difficult path of the enemy;

children.text: satyaprītividhānadakṣa vijayaprāgbhāvabhīma prabho sāmrājyaṃ varavīra vatsaraśataṃ vairiñcamuccaiḥ kriyāḥ' //
children.translated_text: O one skilled in establishing true affection, O <s>Bhīma</s> (terrible one) who is the antecedent of victory, O lord! May your imperial sovereignty, O best of heroes, extend for a hundred years—supreme and exalted rites!'

children.text: atra tvameva haṃsa ityāropaṇapūrvako mānasameva mānasamityādyāropa iti śliṣṭaśabdaṃ mālāparamparitam /
children.translated_text: Here, the superimposition 'you yourself are the swan' is followed by the superimposition 'the mind (<s>mānasa</s>) is indeed the lake <s>Mānasa</s>'—thus it is a garland chain-<s>rūpaka</s> based on words with double meaning.
'With mind, speech, and body I take refuge in the compassionate <s>Jagannātha</s> (lord of the world),
the pair of feet of <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>)—the raft for crossing the ocean of birth, old age, and death.'
'The couch of royal fortune, a wave of the ocean of valor, made of green emeralds, a strip of ichor-water from the elephant of fierce victory that shattered enemy lineages;
a dark rain-cloud above the swan of the fame of enemy lords who wilt in terror of battle—the sword of the <s>Indra</s> of <s>Mālavā</s> is victorious in combat!'

children.text:
atra kṣmāsauvidalla iti paramparitamapyekadeśavivarti /
evamādayo 'nye 'pi bhedā leśataḥ sūcitā eva /
children.translated_text: Here, 'kṣmā-sauvidalla' (sword of the earth / cleaver of the earth) is chain-like yet also an <s>ekadeśa-vivarti</s> (extending to only a portion). Thus and other varieties have been briefly indicated.
As follows—

'A desert of the water of generosity, a wall-painting of the sky of good conduct, a dark fourteenth night of the moonlight of virtues, a bristle of a dog's tail compared to the straightness of <s>yoga</s>—

children.text: yaireṣāpi durāśayā kaliyuge rājāvalī sevitā teṣāṃ śūlini bhaktimātrasulabhe sevā kiyatkauśalam' //
children.translated_text: by those who even in the age of <s>Kali</s> served this line of evil-minded kings—what great skill is their service to You, O <s>Śūlin</s> (Trident-bearer, <s>Śiva</s>), who are attainable by mere devotion!'
This [<s>rūpaka</s>] is also seen through dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>).

children.text: atra cāropyamāṇasya dharmitvādāviṣṭaliṅgasaṃkhyātve 'pi kvacitsvato 'saṃbhavatsaṃkhyāyogasyāpi viṣayasaṃkhyātvam pratyekamāropāt /

children.translated_text: As in: 'Somewhere, matted-haired, bark-clad, cheeks [like] forest fires,' etc.
For the sage <s>Kapila</s> is not multiple.
'Confusion, loss of consciousness, the darkness of bodily decay,

children.text: maraṇaṃ ca jaladabhujagajaṃ prasahya kurute viṣaṃ viyoginīnām' //
children.translated_text: and death like a water-snake—poison forcibly effects all these in women suffering from separation.'

Here, although the superimposed entity has specific gender and number expressed through its own characteristics, sometimes, when its own number is impossible, the number of the subject [is adopted] through individual superimposition.

children.text:
ityatra niyatasaṃkhyākakāryaviśeṣotthāpito garalārthaprabhāvito viṣaśabde śleṣa eva /
jaladabhujagajamiti rūpakasādhakamiti pūrve siddhatvābhāvānna tannicanvanaṃ viṣaśabde śliṣṭaśabdaṃ paramparitamiti śleṣa evātretyāhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, in the word 'poison' (<s>viṣa</s>), which evokes through the specific effects of a fixed number [of symptoms] the potency of venom, there is simply <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning). 'Like a water-snake' is what establishes the <s>rūpaka</s>—the earlier authorities say that since it was not previously established, it is not to be construed as [part of the metaphor]; in the word 'poison' it is a chain-<s>rūpaka</s> based on double meaning—thus there is simply <s>śleṣa</s> here, they say.
START Sūtra 17:
When the superimposed entity has utility for the subject (<s>prakṛta</s>), [the figure is] <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation). || 17 ||

children.text:
āropyamāṇaṃ rūpake prakṛtopayogitvābhāvātprakṛtoparañjakatvenaiva kevalenānvayaṃ bhajate pariṇāme tu prakṛtātmatayā āropyamāṇasyopayoga iti prakṛtamāropyamāṇarūpatvena pariṇamiti /
āgamānugamavigamakhyātyabhāvātsāṃkhyīyapariṇāmavaisakṣaṇyam /
tasya sāmānādhikaraṇyavaiyadhikaraṇyaprayogād dvaividhyam /

children.translated_text: The first, as follows—

'Having crossed the <s>Amaradhunī</s> (celestial Gaṅgā), which is the garland on the crest of <s>Bhūteśa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), He, the third [<s>Rāma</s>], offered to the boatman a raft in the form of friendship with <s>Saumitri</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>).

children.text: vyāmagrāhyastanībhiḥ śabarayuvatibhiḥ kautukodañcadakṣaṃ kṛcchrādanvīyamānastvaritamaya giriṃ citrakūṭaṃ pratasthe' //
children.translated_text: Followed with difficulty by the <s>Śabara</s> tribal women with outstretched breasts, their eyes uplifted in curiosity, He hastily departed for Mount <s>Citrakūṭa</s>.'

In <s>rūpaka</s>, the superimposed entity, lacking utility for the subject, relates to it merely as embellishment. In <s>pariṇāma</s>, however, the superimposed entity has utility as being identical with the subject—thus the subject is transformed into the form of the superimposed entity. Due to the absence of arising (<s>āgama</s>), conformity (<s>anugama</s>), dissolution (<s>vigama</s>), and error (<s>khyāti</s>), it differs from <s>Sāṃkhya</s> [philosophical] transformation. It is twofold, through usage in co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) and in different reference (<s>vaiyadhikaraṇya</s>).

children.text:
atra saumittrimaittrī prakṛtā āropyamāṇasamānādhikaraṇātararūpatvena pariṇatā /
ātarasya maittrīrūpatayā prakṛte upayogāt /
tadatra yathā samāsoktāvāronyamāṇaṃ prakṛtopayogi taccāropaviṣayātmatayā tatra sthitam, ata eva tatra tadvyavahārasamāropaḥ evamihāpi jñeyam, kevalaṃ tatra viṣayasyaiva prayogaḥ, viṣayiṇo gamyamānatvāt /
iha tu dvayorapyabhidhānam, tādātmyāt tu tayoḥ pariṇāmitvam /

children.translated_text: The second, as follows—
'Then, with eloquent words—moist, crooked in path, and approaching maturity—
he first made an offering to the king, and then subsequently with horses and other [gifts].'

Here, the friendship with <s>Saumitri</s> is the subject, which is transformed into the form of a raft (<s>ātara</s>) in co-reference. Because the raft has utility for the subject in the form of friendship. Thus here, just as in <s>samāsokta</s> (compressed expression) the superimposed entity has utility for the subject and abides there by virtue of being the subject of superimposition—and therefore there is a superimposition of its designation—so too it should be understood here; the only difference is that there, only the subject is expressed while the superimposed entity is implied, whereas here both are expressed, and due to their identity, there is transformation.

children.text:
rājasaṃghaṭane tūpāyanamucitam /
taccātra vacorūpamiti vacasāṃ vyadhikaraṇopāyanarūpatvena pariṇāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: An offering is appropriate in the context of meeting a king. And here, the speeches take the form of an offering in a different referent (<s>vyadhikaraṇa</s>)—thus [there is] <s>pariṇāma</s> (transformation).
START Sūtra 18:
When the subject is in a state of being doubted, [the figure is] <s>saṃdeha</s> (doubt). || 18 ||

children.text:
'abhedaprādhānye āropa ityeva /
viṣayaḥ prakṛto 'rtaḥ, yadbhittitvenāprakṛtaḥ saṃdihyate /
aprakṛte saṃdehe viṣayo 'pi saṃdihyata eva /
tena prakṛtāprakṛtagatatvena kavipratibhotthāpite saṃdehe saṃdehālaṅkāraḥ' /
children.translated_text: 'When non-difference is predominant, there is superimposition. The subject is the primary meaning; the non-primary entity is doubted as its substratum. When there is doubt about the non-primary, the subject too is doubted. Thus, when doubt is aroused by the poet's imagination regarding both the primary and the non-primary, [there is] the figure of <s>saṃdeha</s> (doubt).'

children.text:
sa ca trividhaḥ /
śuddho niścayagarbho niścayāntaśca /
śuddho yatra saṃśaya eva paryavasānam /

children.translated_text: As follows—

children.text: 'kiṃ tāruṇyataroriyaṃ rasabharodbhinnā navā vallarī līlāprocchalitasya kiṃ laharikā lāvaṇyavārāṃnidheḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Is this a new creeper burst forth with the weight of sap from the tree of youth? Is this a wavelet of the playfully surging ocean of beauty?

children.text: udgāḍhotkalikāvatāṃ svasamayopanyāsavistrambhiṇaḥ kiṃ sākṣādupadeśayaṣṭirathavā devasya śṛṅgāriṇaḥ' //
children.translated_text: Is this indeed the teaching-staff of the god of <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic love), whose buds are fully swollen, who displays confidence in his own season—or [what is this maiden]?'
It is of three kinds: pure (<s>śuddha</s>), containing certainty (<s>niścaya-garbha</s>), and ending in certainty (<s>niścayānta</s>). 'Pure' is where doubt alone is the conclusion.
As follows—

children.text: 'ayaṃ mārtaṇḍaḥ kiṃ sa khalu turagaiḥ satpabhiritaḥ kṛśānuḥ kiṃ sākṣātprasarati diśo naiṣa niyatam /
children.translated_text: 'Is this the sun? But he has only seven horses. Is this fire itself spreading in the directions? No, certainly not. Is this Death himself riding a buffalo?'—thus for a long time,

children.text: kṛtāntaḥ kiṃ sākṣānmahiṣavahano 'sāviti cirāt samalokyājau tvāṃ vidadhati vikalpānpratibhaṭāḥ' //
children.translated_text: having observed you in battle, the enemies entertain various conjectures.'
'Containing certainty' is that which begins with doubt, has certainty in the middle, and ends in doubt.

children.text: niścayānto yatra saṃśaya upakramo niścaye paryavasānam /

children.translated_text: As follows—

children.text: 'induḥ kiṃ kva kalaṅkaḥ sarasijametatkimambu kutra gatam /
children.translated_text: 'Is this the moon? Where then is the dark spot? Is this a lotus? Where then has the water gone?
With charming and playful words, O doe-eyed one, it is concluded thereafter that [this] is indeed [your] face.'
'Ending in certainty' is where doubt is the beginning and certainty is the conclusion.
As follows—

children.text: 'rañjitā nu vividhāstaruśailā nāmitaṃ tu gaganaṃ mthagitaṃ nu /
children.translated_text: 'Are the various trees and mountains colored? Is the sky bowed down?

children.text: pūritā nu viṣameṣu dharitrī saṃhṛtā nu kakubhastimireṇa' //
children.translated_text: Is the earth filled in the uneven places? Are the directions gathered up—by darkness?'
Sometimes, the superimposed entities are seen as having different substrates.

children.text:
atrāropaviṣaye timire rāgādi tarvādibhinnāśrayatvenāropitam /
kecittvadhyavasāyāśrayatvena saṃdehaprakāramāhuḥ /
anye tu nuśabdasya saṃbhāvanādyotatvādutprekṣāprakāramimamācakṣate /
children.translated_text: Here, upon the subject of superimposition, namely darkness, color and other [qualities] are superimposed with different substrates such as trees and others. Some, however, describe this as a variety of <s>saṃdeha</s> on the basis of determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>). Others explain this as a variety of <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), since the particle 'nu' indicates supposition.
START Sūtra 19:
The apprehension of another entity due to resemblance is <s>bhrāntimān</s> (mistaken perception). || 19 ||

children.text:
asamyagjñānatvasādharmyātsaṃdehānantaramasya lakṣaṇam /
bhrāntiścittadharmaḥ /
sa vidyate yasminbhaṇitiprakāre sa bhrāntimān /
sādṛśyaprayuktā ca bhrāntirasya viṣayaḥ /

children.translated_text: For example:

children.text: 'oṣṭhe bimbaphalāśayālamalakeṣūtpākajambūdhiyā karṇolaṅkṛtibhāji dāḍimaphalabhrāntyā ca śoṇe bhaṇau /
children.translated_text: 'On the lips, with the appearance of <s>bimba</s> fruits; on the dark locks, with the notion of ripe <s>jambū</s> berries; on the ear ornaments, with the delusion of pomegranate fruits; and on the red cheeks,

children.text: niṣpattyā sakṛdutpalacchadadṛśāmāttaklamānāṃ marau rājangṛrjararājapañjaraśukaiḥ sadyastṛṣā mūrcchitam' //
children.translated_text: at the sight of eyes resembling <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus) petals, weary travelers on the desert were instantly overcome with thirst — by the parrots in the cage of the king of <s>Gūrjara</s>!'

Because of the common property of being imperfect knowledge, the definition of this [<s>bhrāntimān</s>] follows immediately after <s>saṃdeha</s> (doubt). <s>Bhrānti</s> (delusion) is a property of the mind. That manner of expression in which it is present is called <s>bhrāntimān</s> (possessed of delusion). And the delusion caused by resemblance is its subject matter.
For example:
'By <s>Cāṇūra</s> the wrestler, whose entire chest was crushed by the blow of <s>Dāmodara</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>),
a hundred moons were seen in the sky.'
However, delusion caused by a severe blow to a vital spot and the like is not the subject of this <s>alaṅkāra</s>.

children.text:
sādṛśyahetukāpi bhrāntirvicchittyarthe kavipratibhotthāpitaiva gṛhyate,yathodāhṛtam, na svarasotthāpitā śuktikārajatavat /
evaṃ sthāṇurvā syātpuruṣo vā syāditi saṃśaye 'pi boddhavyam /
children.translated_text: Even delusion caused by resemblance is understood [in this <s>alaṅkāra</s>] only when evoked by the poet's imagination for the purpose of aesthetic charm (<s>vicchitti</s>), as illustrated [above], not when arising naturally like the [mistaken perception of] silver in a shell. The same should be understood regarding doubt such as 'Is it a post or a person?'
START Sūtra 20:
The apprehension of even one [thing] in multiple ways due to different causes is <s>ullekha</s> (multiple description). // RuAss 20 //

children.text:
yatraikaṃ vastvanekadhā gṛhyate sa rūpabāhulyollekhanādullekhaḥ /
na cedaṃ nirnimittamullekhamātram, api tu nānāvidhadharmayogitvākhyanimittavaśādetatkriyate /
tatra rucyarthitvavyutpattayo yathāyogaṃ prayojikāḥ /

children.translated_text: As it is stated:
'According to inclination, according to purpose, and according to understanding,
the appearance of even one thing is differentiated when investigation is accomplished.'

Where one thing is apprehended in multiple ways — that is <s>ullekha</s>, so called from the delineation of multiplicity of forms. And this is not causeless mere description; rather it is done by virtue of a cause called the possession of various properties. In this, inclination (<s>ruci</s>), purpose (<s>arthitva</s>), and understanding (<s>vyutpatti</s>) are the motivating factors, as appropriate.
Thus.

children.text:
yathā-
'yastapovanamit.i munibhiḥ kāmāyatanamiti veśyābhiḥ saṃgītaśāleti lāsakaiḥ' ityādi harṣacarite śrīkaṇṭhākhyajanapadavarṇane /
atra hyeka eva śrīkaṇṭhākhyojanapadastattadguṇayogāttapovanādyanekarūpatayā nirūpitaḥ /
ruccarthitvavyutpattayaśca prāyaśaḥ samastavyastā yojayituṃ śakyante /
nanvetanmadhye 'vajravañjaramiti śaraṇāgatairasuravivaramiti vātikaiḥ' ityādau rūpakālaṅkārayoga iti kathamayamullekhālaṅkāraviṣayaḥ /
satyam /
asti tāvat 'tapovanam' ityādau rūpakavivikto 'sya viṣayaḥ /
yatra vastutastadrūpatāyāḥ saṃbhavaḥ /
yatra tu rūpakaṃ vyavasthitaṃ tatra cediyamapi bhaṅgiḥ saṃbhāvinī tatsaṃkaro 'stu /
na tvetāvatāsyābhāvaḥ śakyate vaktum /
tataśca na doṣaḥ kaścit /
evaṃ hi tatra viṣaye bhrāntimadalaṅkāro 'stu atadrūpasya tadrūpatāpratītinibandhanatvāt /
naitat /
anaikadhāgrahaṇākhyasyāpūrvasyātiśayasyābhāvāt, taddhetukatvāccāsyālaṅkārasya /
saṃkarapratītistvaṅgīkṛtaiva yadyevam, abhede bheda ityevaṃrūpātiśayoktiratrāstu /

children.translated_text: This is not a fault.

children.text: grahītṛbhedākhyena viṣayavibhāgenānekadhātvoṭṭaṅkanāttasya ca vicchittyantararūpatvāt sarvathā nāsyāntarbhāvaḥ śakyakriya iti niścayaḥ /
children.translated_text: By the division of subject-matter called 'difference of apprehenders,' and because the multiple apprehension is stamped [with that distinction], and because it is of the nature of a different kind of aesthetic charm (<s>vicchitti</s>), it is determined that its inclusion [in another figure] is impossible in any way.

children.text: yathā vā- 'ṇārāaṇot ti pariṇaavaāhiṃ sirivallahot ti taruṇīhiṃ /
children.translated_text: Or for example: 'As <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> by the mature in age, as the beloved of <s>Śrī</s> by the young women,

children.text: bālāhiṃ uṇa kodūhaleṇa eme a saccavio' //
children.translated_text: by the children, moreover, with curiosity — thus indeed authenticated.'

For example: 'As a penance grove by the sages, as an abode of desire by the courtesans, as a concert hall by the dancers' — and so on, in the description of the country called <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> in <s>Harṣacarita</s>. Here, one and the same country called <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> is described in multiple forms — as a penance grove, etc. — due to its possession of various qualities. And inclination, purpose, and understanding can generally be applied, severally or collectively. Objection: Among these, in passages like 'as a diamond-cage by the refugees, as a demon-cave by the madmen' — there is the presence of the <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) <s>alaṅkāra</s>; so how is this a subject of the <s>ullekha</s> <s>alaṅkāra</s>? True. But in 'penance grove' etc., the subject of this [<s>ullekha</s>] is distinct from <s>rūpaka</s> — where the actual identity with that form is possible. But where <s>rūpaka</s> is established and this mode of expression is also possible, let there be a combination (<s>saṃkara</s>). This does not mean that its [<s>ullekha</s>'s] existence cannot be asserted. Therefore there is no fault. For in that very subject, let there also be the <s>bhrāntimān</s> <s>alaṅkāra</s>, since it is based on the cognition of what-is-not-that as that. No — because of the absence of the unprecedented excellence (<s>atiśaya</s>) called 'multiple apprehension,' and because this <s>alaṅkāra</s> is caused by that [excellence]. The cognition of combination is indeed accepted; if so, let there be <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) of the form 'difference in non-difference.'
[Sanskrit rendering:] 'As <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> by those of mature age, as the beloved of <s>Śrī</s> by the young women,
by the children, moreover, with curiosity — thus indeed authenticated.'

children.text:
evam
'garurvacasi pṛthururasi arjuno yaśasi' ityādāvavaseyam /
iyāṃstu viśeṣaḥ-pūrvatra grahītṛbhedenānekadhātvollekhaḥ, iha tu viṣayabhedena /
nanvanekadhātvollekhane gurvādirūpatayā śleṣa iti kathamalaṅkārāntaramatra sthāpyate /
satyam /
anekadhātvanimittaṃ tu vicchittyantaramatra dṛśyate iti tatpratibhotpattihetuḥ śleṣo 'tra syāt /
na tu sarvathā tadabhāvaḥ /
ataścālaṅkārāntaraṃ yadevaṃvidhe viṣaye śleṣābhāve 'pi vicchittisadbhāvaḥ /
tasmādevamādāvullekha eva śreyān /
evamalaṅkārāntaravicchittyāśrayeṇāpyayamalaṅkāro nidarśanīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Similarly, in passages like 'weighty in speech, broad in chest, brilliant (<s>Arjuna</s>) in fame' — the same should be understood. But here the distinction is: in the former [example], the <s>ullekha</s> is through difference of apprehenders; here, however, it is through difference of subject-matter. Objection: In the multiple apprehension as 'weighty' etc., <s>śleṣa</s> (double entendre) is present; so how is a different <s>alaṅkāra</s> established here? True. But a different kind of aesthetic charm is seen here as the cause of the multiple apprehension. So <s>śleṣa</s> may be present as the cause of generating the cognition of [this <s>alaṅkāra</s>]; but this does not mean its [<s>ullekha</s>'s] complete absence. Therefore it is a different <s>alaṅkāra</s>, because even in the absence of <s>śleṣa</s> in such a subject, aesthetic charm exists. Hence, in such cases <s>ullekha</s> alone is preferable. Thus this <s>alaṅkāra</s> should be illustrated with reference to the aesthetic charm of other <s>alaṅkāras</s> as well.
START Sūtra 21:
The denial of the subject [of comparison] is <s>apahnuti</s> (concealment/denial). // RuAss 21 //

children.text:
vastvantarapratītirityeva prakrāntāpahnavavaidharmyeṇedamucyate /
āropaprastāvādāropaviṣayāpahnutāvāropyamāṇapratītāvapahnutyākhyo 'laṃṅkāraḥ /
tasya ca trayī bandhacchāyā, apahnavapūrvaka āropaḥ, āropapūrvako 'pahnavaḥ /
chalādiśabdairasatyatvapratipādakairvāpahnavanirdeśaḥ /
pūrvoktabhedadvaye vākyabhedaḥ /
tṛtīyabhede tvekavākyatvam /

children.translated_text: The first [variety], for example:

children.text: 'yadetaccandrāntarjaladalavalīlāṃ prakurute tadācaṣṭe lokaḥ śaśaka iti no māṃ prati tathā /
children.translated_text: 'That what appears as a mark inside the moon creates the semblance of a lotus-leaf — the world calls it "hare" — but not so for me.
I think it rather the scar from the wound of the firebrand-glance of a young woman afflicted by the pain of separation from your enemy,

Since the cognition of another thing has been [previously] introduced, this is stated with the distinction of denial. In the context of superimposition (<s>āropa</s>), when the object of superimposition is denied and the superimposed [thing] is cognized, the <s>alaṅkāra</s> called <s>apahnuti</s> [arises]. And it has three varieties of construction: denial preceding superimposition; superimposition preceding denial; and denial expressed through words like 'pretext' (<s>chala</s>) that convey unreality. In the first two varieties, there is a separation of sentences. In the third variety, however, there is unity of sentence.

children.text: atraindavasya śaśasyāpahnave upakṣitpe śaśakaprativastukiṇavata indorāropo nānvayaghaṭanāṃ puṣyatīti na niravadyam /
children.translated_text: Here, the denial of the [moon-]hare and the superimposition of the scar on the moon as a counterpart do not support the logical construction well — hence it is not faultless.

children.text: tattu yathā 'pūrṇendoḥ paripoṣakāntavapuṣaḥ sphāraprabhābhāsvaraṃ nedaṃ maṇḍalamabhyayudeni gaganābhoge jigīṣorjagat /
children.translated_text: But [a good example] is: 'This is not the disc of the full moon, beautiful with the loveliness of nurture, brilliant with spreading splendor, wishing to conquer the world, rising in the expanse of the sky.
It is the raised white parasol of <s>Bhāra</s> (the earth-bearer), resplendent with the beauty of its white surface — the sole instrument of effort in destroying the pride of the arrogant.'
The second [variety], for example:
'He who always dwells above the hosts of blue lotuses that are the eyes of the celestial maidens, keeping [them] subdued through restraint —

children.text: na tu rucirakalāpe vartate yo mayūre vitaratu sa kumāro brahmacaryaśriyaṃ vaḥ' //
children.translated_text: it is not that he abides on the beautiful peacock; may that <s>Kumāra</s> (<s>Kārttikeya</s>) bestow upon you the glory of celibacy!'
The third [variety], for example:
'The pearls falling from the swaying beautiful garland-vines on the violently trembling, high breasts of the <s>Gūrjara</s> women who abandoned their houses in panic from the earthquake,

children.text: sārdhaṃ tvadripubhistvadīyaśasāṃ śūnye marau dhāvatāṃ bhraṣṭaṃ rājamṛgāṅkaṃ! kundamukulasthūlaiḥ śramāmbhaḥkaṇaiḥ' //
children.translated_text: as they ran with your enemies in the empty desert, [pursuing] your fame — they are [merely] drops of perspiration, O king, thick as <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) buds, [coming from] the moon-mark [on the banner]!'

children.text:
atra śūnya ityasya sthāne manyeśabdaprayoge sāpahnavotprekṣā ittayapi sthāpayiṣyate, ' ahaṃ tvinduṃ manye ' iti tu vākyabhede manyeśabdaprayogenotprekṣeti ca vakṣyate /
etasminnapi bhedo 'pahnavāropayoḥ paurvāparyaprayogaviparyaye bhedadvayaṃ sadapi na pūrvavaccitratāvahamiti na bhedatvena gaṇitam /
tatrāpahnuvapūrvake ārope nirantaramudāhṛtam /

children.translated_text: In the [type with] superimposition preceding denial, for example:
'White with the smearing of moonlight-ash, wearing star-bones, fond of the sport of disappearing, this <s>Kātrikā-pālikī</s> (skull-bearing female ascetic) [who is] the Night —

children.text: dvīpāddvīpaṃ bhramati dadhatī candramudākāpāne nyastaṃ siddhāñjanaparimalaṃ lāñcanasya cchalena' //
children.translated_text: she wanders from island to island, bearing a moon-bowl for collecting alms, applying the fragrance of perfected <s>añjana</s> (collyrium) [as the darkness] under the pretext of the moon-mark.'

Here, if in place of 'empty' (<s>śūnya</s>) one uses the word 'I think' (<s>manye</s>), it would be <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) with concealment — as will also be established [later]. And in 'I think it the moon-mark' — with the use of <s>manye</s> in a separate sentence — it will be stated to be <s>utprekṣā</s>. Even in this [<s>apahnuti</s>], the variety [arises from] the reversal of the sequence of denial and superimposition; yet when there are two varieties based on such reversal, since they do not produce the same [degree of] aesthetic charm as the previous [varieties], they are not counted as [separate] varieties. In the [type with] denial preceding superimposition, [examples] have been continuously given.
Sometimes, the unreality [of the denied thing] is expressed through words like 'body' (<s>vapus</s>) that denote being of the nature of another thing. For example:

children.text: 'amuṣmiṃllāvaṇyāmṛtasarasi nūnaṃ mṛgadṛśaḥ smaraḥ śarvapluṣṭaḥ pṛthujaghanabhāge nipatitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In this lake of the nectar of her beauty, surely <s>Smara</s> (the god of love), burnt by <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), fell upon the region of her broad hips.

children.text: yadaṅgāṅgārāṇāṃ praśamapiśunā nābhikuhare khikhā dhūmasyeyaṃ pariṇamati romāvalivapuḥ' //
children.translated_text: For the line of body-hair, in the form of a streak of smoke indicating the cooling of [his] body-embers, develops in the cave of her navel.'
Thus.
START Sūtra 22:

Having thus defined the <s>alaṅkāras</s> containing superimposition (<s>āropa</s>) within the [domain of] predominance of non-difference, he now defines those containing <s>adhyavasāya</s> (identification/determination):
When identification (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) predominates and the function (<s>vyāpāra</s>) is predominant, it is <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy). // RuAss 22 //
The cognition of non-difference through the absorption of the subject [into the predicate] is <s>adhyavasāya</s> (identification).

children.text:
sa ca dvividhaḥ - sādhyaḥ siddhaśca /
sādhyo yatra viṣayiṇo 'satyatayā pratītiḥ /
asatyatvaṃ ca viṣayigatasya dharmasya viṣaya upanibandhe viṣayisaṃbhāvitvena viṣayāsaṃbhāvitvena ca pratīteḥ /
dharmo,guṇakriyārūpaḥ tasya saṃbhavāsaṃbhavapratītau saṃbhavāśrayasya tatrāparamārthatayā asatyatvaṃ pratīyate, itarasya tu paramārthatayā satyatvam /
yasyāsatyatvaṃ, tasya satyatvapratītāvadhyavasāyaḥ sādhyaḥ /
ataśca vyāpāraprādhānyam /
siddho yatra viṣayiṇo vastuto 'satyasyāpi satyatāpratītiḥ /
satvatvaṃ ca pūrvakasyāsatyatvanimittasyabhāvāt /
ataścādhyavasitaprādhānyam /

pratīyamānāyāṃ punarivādyaprayogaḥ /
sā ca jātikriyāguṇadravyatāṇāmaprakṛtānāmadhyavaseyatvena caturthā /
prakṛtasyaitadbhedayoge 'pi na vaicitryamiti na te gaṇitāḥ /

eṣā gatirvācyotprekṣāyā /

pratīyamānāyāstu yadyapyuddeśata etāvantobhedāḥ, tathāpi nimittasyānupādānaṃ tasyāṃ na saṃbhavatīti tairbhedair yūno 'yaṃ prakāraḥ /
ivādyanupādāne nimittasyata cākīrtane utprekṣaṇasya niṣpamāṇatvāt /
prāyaśca svarūpotprakṣāyā yathāsaṃbhavaṃ bhedanirdeśa /
eṣā cārthāśrayati dharmaviṣaye śliṣṭaśabdahetukā kvacitpadārthānvayavelāyāṃ sādṛśyābhivānādupakrāntāpyupamāvākyārthatātparyasāmarythābhimantṛvyāpāropārohakrameṇotprekṣāyāṃ paryavasyati /
kvacicchalādiśabdaprayoge sāpahnavātprekṣā bhavati /
ataścoktavakṣyamāṇaprakāravaicitryeṇānantyamasyāḥ /
children.translated_text:
And that [<s>adhyavasāya</s> (determinative identification)] is of two kinds: <s>sādhya</s> (to-be-established) and <s>siddha</s> (already established).
<s>Sādhya</s> is where there is a cognition of the unreality of the <s>viṣayin</s> (subject/identified-with). The unreality consists in the fact that, when a property belonging to the <s>viṣayin</s> is superimposed upon the <s>viṣaya</s> (object/locus), the cognition arises both through the possibility of the <s>viṣayin</s> [possessing that property] and through the impossibility of the <s>viṣaya</s> [possessing it].
The property is in the form of <s>guṇa</s> (quality) or <s>kriyā</s> (action); when there is cognition of its possibility and impossibility, the substrate of possibility is cognized as unreal therein due to its non-ultimate nature, while the other [substrate] is cognized as real due to its ultimate nature.
That whose unreality is [made to appear as if real] — the cognition of its reality constitutes <s>sādhya adhyavasāya</s> (to-be-established identification).
Hence [in this type] the predominance belongs to the <s>vyāpāra</s> (cognitive operation).
<s>Siddha</s> (established) is where there is a cognition of reality regarding the <s>viṣayin</s> which is in fact unreal.
The reality [arises] because the prior cause of unreality is absent.
Hence [in this type] the predominance belongs to the <s>adhyavasita</s> (the thing identified).
There, when the cognition is of the to-be-established type, with predominance of the cognitive operation, the <s>adhyavasāya</s> is denoted by words such as <s>saṃbhāvanā</s> (supposition), <s>abhimāna</s> (imaginative attribution), <s>tarka</s> (conjecture), <s>ūha</s> (surmise), <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), and so on.
Thus, <s>utprekṣā</s> is the imaginative identification of the <s>prakṛta</s> (primary subject) as being something non-primary, by virtue of its connection with qualities and actions belonging to the non-primary.
The <s>vācya</s> (expressed) [type] is indicated by particles such as <s>iva</s> (as if).
In the <s>pratīyamānā</s> (suggested) [type], however, particles like <s>iva</s> are not employed.
It is fourfold according to what is imaginatively identified among non-primary entities: <s>jāti</s> (class), <s>kriyā</s> (action), <s>guṇa</s> (quality), and <s>dravya</s> (substance).
Even though the <s>prakṛta</s> (primary subject) can be connected with these subdivisions, there is no [additional] variety thereby, and so those are not counted separately.
For each [of the four], there is a twofold division according to whether the imaginative attribution is of presence or absence [of the property], yielding eight varieties.
For each of the eight varieties, the <s>nimitta</s> (ground/reason) being in the form of either <s>guṇa</s> (quality) or <s>kriyā</s> (action) yields sixteen subdivisions.
For each of those, the ground being either stated or unstated yields thirty-two sub-varieties; and for each of those, the imaginative identification being in the form of <s>hetu</s> (cause), <s>svarūpa</s> (essential nature), or <s>phala</s> (result) yields ninety-six varieties.
This is the scope of <s>vācya utprekṣā</s> (expressed poetic fancy).
Among these, since <s>dravya</s> (substance) mostly involves only <s>svarūpa utprekṣā</s> (fancy of essential nature), the subdivisions of <s>hetu utprekṣā</s> (fancy of cause) and <s>phala utprekṣā</s> (fancy of result) should be excluded from it.
As for <s>pratīyamānā</s> (suggested poetic fancy), although nominally it has this many subdivisions, nevertheless since the non-statement of the <s>nimitta</s> (ground) is not possible in it, [the total] varieties of this type are fewer by those subdivisions.
Because in the absence of particles like <s>iva</s> and also without mentioning the ground, the <s>utprekṣā</s> cannot be accomplished.
Mostly, the subdivision-specification of <s>svarūpa utprekṣā</s> applies as appropriate.
This [<s>utprekṣā</s>], being grounded in meaning and pertaining to properties, sometimes — when occasioned by a <s>śliṣṭa</s> (equivocal) word, at the juncture of construing word-meanings — even though initiated through the expression of similarity as in <s>upamā</s> (simile), culminates in <s>utprekṣā</s> through the ascending sequence of the sentence-meaning, purport, capability, and the cognitive operation of the attributor.
Sometimes, when words like <s>chala</s> (pretext) are employed, it becomes <s>utprekṣā</s> combined with <s>apahṇava</s> (denial/concealment).
Hence, through the variety of modes — both those already stated and those yet to be stated — this [figure] has infinite [varieties].
Among these, <s>jāti utprekṣā</s> (fancy of class), for example:

children.text: 'sa vaḥ pāyādindurnavabisalatākoṭikuṭilaḥ- smārāreryo mūrdhni jvalanakapiśo bhāti nihitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'May that <s>Indu</s> (moon) protect you — curved like the tip of a fresh lotus stalk, blazing tawny with fire, placed upon the head of the enemy of <s>Smara</s> (i.e., <s>Śiva</s>),

children.text: stravanmandākinyāḥ pratidivasasiktena payasā kapālenonmuktaḥ sphaṭikadhavalenāṅkura iva' //
children.translated_text: daily watered by the flowing waters of the <s>Mandākinī</s> (heavenly Ganges) — [appearing] like a sprout emerging from a skull white as crystal.'
Now this [<s>utprekṣā</s>] will be illustrated in brief.
Here, since the word <s>aṅkura</s> (sprout) is a class-denoting word, it is the <s>jāti</s> (class) that is imaginatively identified.
<s>Kriyā utprekṣā</s> (fancy of action), for example:
'Darkness smears the limbs, as it were; the sky rains down collyrium, as it were.'
Here the actions of smearing and raining are imaginatively identified as belonging to darkness and the sky respectively.
In the latter half, however: 'vision has attained fruitlessness, like the service of a wicked person' —
<s>Guṇa utprekṣā</s> (fancy of quality), for example:

children.text: 'saiṣā sthalī yatra vicinvatā tvāṃ bhraṣṭaṃ mayā nūpuramekamurvyām /
children.translated_text: 'This is the ground where, while searching for you, one of my anklets fell upon the earth;
it appeared to have assumed silence, as if from the grief of separation from your lotus-feet.'
in this, it is only <s>upamā</s> (simile), not <s>utprekṣā</s>.
<s>Dravya utprekṣā</s> (fancy of substance), for example:
'Seeing this netherworld empty of <s>Mṛgalāñchana</s> (the moon), [bereft of] the festival for the eyes,
the women here have created, as it were, a moon-filled world in the sky, using the pretext of their own faces.'
Here, <s>duḥkha</s> (grief) is the <s>guṇa</s> (quality).

children.text:
atra candrasyaikatvād dravyatvam /
etāni bhāvābhimāne udāharaṇāni /
children.translated_text:
Here, since the moon is a single entity, it has the nature of <s>dravya</s> (substance).
These are examples of <s>bhāva abhimāna</s> (imaginative attribution of presence).
In [the case of] <s>abhāva abhimāna</s> (imaginative attribution of absence), for example:
'Her cheek-surfaces, alas, having become such [i.e., emaciated],
as if not seeing each other, have attained such thinness.'

children.text:
atrāpaśyantāviti kriyāyā abhāvābhimānaḥ /
evaṃ jātyādāvapyūdyam /
guṇasya nimittatvaṃ yathā-
'navabisalatākoṭikuṭilaḥ' ityatrodāhṛte kuṭilatvasya /
kriyāyā yathā- r'idṛkṣāṃ kṣāmatāṃ gatau' ityatra kṣāmatāgamanasya /
nimittopādānasyaite udāharaṇe /

children.translated_text: For [the case where the ground is] unstated, the verse 'Darkness smears the limbs, as it were' and so on serves as the example.
<s>Hetu utprekṣā</s> (fancy of cause), for example: 'as if having assumed silence from the grief of separation' and so on.

children.text: svārūpotprekṣā yathā - 'kuberajuṣṭāṃ diśamuṣṇaraśmau gantuṃ pravṛtte samayaṃ vilaṅghya /
children.translated_text: <s>Svarūpa utprekṣā</s> (fancy of essential nature), for example: 'When the hot-rayed one (<s>Sūrya</s>) set forth to travel toward the direction presided over by <s>Kubera</s>, transgressing the proper course,

children.text: dig dakṣiṇā gandhavahaṃ mukhena vyalīkaniḥ śvāsamivotsasarja' //
children.translated_text: the southern direction, as it were, released a sigh of displeasure through the mouth of the wind.'

Here, 'not seeing' is the imaginative attribution of the absence of an action.
The same should be understood for <s>jāti</s> (class) and the rest as well.
The <s>guṇa</s> (quality) serving as the <s>nimitta</s> (ground), for example:
in the verse cited above, 'curved like the tip of a fresh lotus stalk' — here <s>kuṭilatva</s> (curvedness) [is the ground].
The <s>kriyā</s> (action) [serving as the ground], for example: in 'have attained such thinness' — here the attainment of thinness [is the ground].
These are examples where the <s>nimitta</s> (ground) is stated.

children.text: phalotprekṣā yathā - 'colasya yadbhītipalāyitasya bhālatvacaṃ kaṇṭakino vanāntāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Phala utprekṣā</s> (fancy of result), for example: 'The thorny forest-edges [tore] the forehead-skin of the <s>Cola</s> king who had fled in fear —
even now, as if to see whether he will experience [more suffering], they split open [the skin] to read the letters [of fate].'
<s>Pratīyamānā utprekṣā</s> (suggested poetic fancy), for example:
'<s>mahilāsahasabharie tuha hiae suhaa sā asāmantī</s> /
<s>aṇudiṇamaṇaṇṇaambhā aṅgaṃ taṇuaṃpi taṇuei</s>' //
Thus, the direction of examples for <s>vācya utprekṣā</s> (expressed poetic fancy) has been given.
(Sanskrit <s>chāyā</s>: '<s>mahilāsahasrabharite tava hṛdaye subhaga sā asamāntī</s> /
<s>anudinam ananyakarmā aṅgaṃ tanukam api tanayati</s>') //

children.text:
atra-
amāantītyavartamāneveti tanūkaraṇahetutvenotprekṣitam /
evaṃ bhedāntareṣvapi jñeyam /
children.translated_text:
Here:
'<s>asamāntī</s>' means 'not finding room' — the thinning [of the body] is imaginatively identified as being caused by [her] not finding room [in his heart full of thousands of women].
The same should be understood in the other subdivisions as well.

[<s>Utprekṣā</s>] occasioned by an equivocal word (<s>śliṣṭa śabda</s>), for example: 'He who is celebrated on the surface of the earth by the title <s>tyāgin</s> (renouncer/generous one), being unequalled in having no equal,
became exceedingly a field for the arrows of <s>Smara</s> (Love), [the arrows] that had gone forth with self-regard.'
Here, with respect to the property, the word <s>mārgaṇa</s> (meaning both 'arrow' and 'seeking') is equivocal (<s>śliṣṭa</s>).

children.text: upamopakramotprekṣā yathā - 'kastūrītilakanti bhālaphalake devyā mukhāmbhoruhe rolambanti tamālabālamukulottaṃsanti maulāvapi /
children.translated_text: <s>Utprekṣā</s> initiated through <s>upamā</s> (simile), for example: 'Upon the forehead-surface of the goddess's lotus-face, they act as musk-<s>tilaka</s>; they hang as <s>tamāla</s>-bud ornaments on her crown;

children.text: yāḥ karṇe vikacotpalanti kucayoraṅke ca kālāguru- sthāsanti prathayantu tāstava śivaṃ śrīkaṇṭhakaṇṭhatviśaṣaḥ' //
children.translated_text: on her ears they serve as full-blown <s>utpala</s> lotuses, and on the region of her breasts as dark <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood) — may those [bees] of <s>Śrīkaṇṭha's</s> (<s>Śiva's</s>) throat bestow auspiciousness upon you.'

children.text:
atra yadyapi 'sarvaprātipadikebhyaḥ kkip' ityupamānātkkibvidhāvāmukhe upamāpratītistathāpyupamānasya prakṛte saṃbhavaucityātsaṃbhāvanotthane utprekṣāyāṃ paryavasānam /
yathā vā virahavaṇaṃne 'keyūrāyitamaṅgadaiḥ' ityādau /
eṣāpi samastopamāpratīpādakaviṣaye 'pi harṣacaritavārtite sāhityamīmāṃsāyāṃ ca teṣu teṣu pradeśeṣudāhṛtā, iha tu granthavistarabhayānna prapañcitā /
children.translated_text:
Here, although by the rule '<s>kkip</s> [is added] to all nominal stems' — when <s>kkip</s> is applied from the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison), there is initially a cognition of <s>upamā</s> (simile) — nevertheless, because of the propriety and possibility of the <s>upamāna</s> being present in the <s>prakṛta</s> (primary subject), [the figure] culminates in <s>utprekṣā</s> through the arising of <s>saṃbhāvanā</s> (supposition).
Similarly, in <s>Virahavarṇana</s> (Description of Separation): '<s>keyūrāyitam aṅgadaiḥ</s>' (the armlets acted as <s>keyūras</s>) and so on.
This [type] has been illustrated in those various passages in the domain of all <s>samasta upamā</s> (compound simile) and <s>pratīpa</s> (reverse simile), in the <s>Harshacarita</s> narrative, and in the <s>Sāhityamīmāṃsā</s>; but here it is not elaborated for fear of expanding the treatise.
<s>Utprekṣā</s> combined with <s>apahṇava</s> (denial/concealment), for example:
'When the city-women rushed to the bank in alarm at the striking of sea-monsters,
the <s>Siprā</s> river shines forth as if laughing with peals of laughter, under the pretext of its surging mass of foam.'

children.text:
atrevaśabdamāhātmyātsaṃbhāvanaṃ chalaśabdaprayogāccāpahnavo gamyate /
evaṃ chadmādiśabdaprayoge 'pi jñeyam /
'apara iva pākaśāsanaḥ' ityādāvaparaśabdāprayoge upamaiveyam /
tatprayoge tu prakṛtasya rājñaḥ pākaśāsanatvapratītāvadhyavasāyasaṃbhāvādivaśabdena ca tasya sādhyatvapratīterutprekṣaiveyam /
ivaśabādāprayoge siddhatvādadhyavasāyasyātiśayoktiḥ /
ivāparaśabdayoraprayoge tu rūpakam /
tadevaṃ prakāravaicitryeṇāvasthitāyā utprekṣāyā hetūtprekṣāyāṃ yasya prakṛtasaṃbandhino dharmasya heturutprekṣate sa dharmo 'dhyavasāyavaśādabhinna utprekṣāyāṃ nimittatvenāśrīyate /
sa ca vācya eva niyamena bhavati /
anyathā kaṃ prati hetuḥ syāt /
yathā-'apaśyantāvivānyonyam' ityādau /
atra kapolayoḥ prakṛtayoḥ saṃbandhitvenopāttasya kṣāmatāgamanasya heturadarśanamutprekṣitam /
hetuphalaṃ ca kṣāmatāgamanaṃ tatra nimittam /
evam 'adṛśyata tvaccaraṇāravindaviśleṣaduḥkhādiva baddhamaunam'ityatra nūpuragatasya maunitvasya heturduḥkhitvam /
tadutprekṣaṇe maunitvameva nimittaṃ jñeyam /
evaṃ sarvatra /
children.translated_text:
Here, by the force of the word <s>iva</s> (as if), <s>saṃbhāvanā</s> (imaginative supposition) is understood, and by the employment of the word <s>chala</s> (pretext), <s>apahṇava</s> (denial/concealment) is understood.
The same should be understood when words like <s>chadma</s> (disguise) and similar terms are employed.
