In [a verse like] '<s>apara iva Pākaśāsanaḥ</s>' (like another <s>Indra</s>) and so on — when the word <s>apara</s> (another) is not employed, this is simply <s>upamā</s> (simile).
But when it is employed, then — because the king who is the <s>prakṛta</s> (primary subject) is cognized as having the nature of <s>Pākaśāsana</s> (<s>Indra</s>) through <s>adhyavasāya</s> (identification), and because the word <s>iva</s> produces the cognition of its being <s>sādhya</s> (to-be-established) — this is indeed <s>utprekṣā</s>.
When the word <s>iva</s> is not employed, since the <s>adhyavasāya</s> is <s>siddha</s> (established), it is <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole).
When neither <s>iva</s> nor <s>apara</s> is employed, it is <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor).
Thus, in <s>utprekṣā</s> as it stands with such variety of modes — in <s>hetu utprekṣā</s> (fancy of cause), whichever property connected with the <s>prakṛta</s> (primary subject) has its cause imaginatively identified, that property serves as the <s>nimitta</s> (ground) in the <s>utprekṣā</s>, being treated as non-different [from the subject] by force of <s>adhyavasāya</s> (identification).
And that [property serving as ground] is necessarily <s>vācya</s> (expressed/stated).
Otherwise, for whom would it serve as the cause?
For example, in 'as if not seeing each other' and so on —
here, for the cheeks which are the <s>prakṛta</s> (primary subjects), the non-seeing is imaginatively identified as the <s>hetu</s> (cause) of the attainment of thinness, which is taken up as connected [with them].
The <s>hetu</s> (cause) and <s>phala</s> (result) — namely the attainment of thinness — serve there as the <s>nimitta</s> (ground).
Similarly, in 'it appeared to have assumed silence, as if from the grief of separation from your lotus-feet' — here, for the silence that belongs to the anklet, the <s>hetu</s> (cause) is grief.
When that [grief] is imaginatively identified, it is the silence itself that should be understood as the <s>nimitta</s> (ground).
The same applies everywhere.

children.text:
svarūpotprekṣāyāṃ yatra dharmī dharmyantaragatatvenotpekṣyate tatrāpi nimittabhūto dharmaḥ kkacinnirdiśyate /
yathā-'sa vaḥ pāyādunduḥ' ityādau /
atra kuṭulatvādi nirdiṣṭameva /
'veleva rāgasāgarasya' ityādau saṃkṣobhakāritvādi gamyamānam /
yatra ca dharma eva dharmigatatvenotprekṣyate tatrāpi nimittasyopādānānupādānābhyam /

children.translated_text: When [the cause] is stated, for example—
'When he attains his consecration, [the enemies'] established power will be destroyed;
the earth trembled, as if bewildered with fear, its commands being abolished.'

In <s>svarūpotprekṣā</s> (fancy about essential nature), where the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) is fancied as being another subject, there too the property serving as the cause (<s>nimitta</s>) is sometimes stated. For example, in 'May that <s>undu</s> protect you,' etc. — here, crookedness and such [properties] are explicitly stated. In 'Like the shore of the ocean of passion,' etc., the capacity to cause agitation is implied. And where a property alone is fancied as belonging to a subject, there too the cause may or may not be stated.

children.text:
atra bhūgatatvena bhayavihvalitatvākhyadharmotprekṣāyāṃ kampādinimittamupāttama /
anupādāne yathā-'lipmatīva tamo 'ṅgāni' ityādau /
atra tamotatatvena lepanakriyākartṛtvopekṣāyāṃ vyāpanādi nimittaṃ gamyamānam /
vyāpanādau tūtprekṣāviṣaye nimittamanyadanveṣyaṃ syāt /
na ca viṣayasya gamyamānatvaṃ yuktam /
tasyotprekṣitādhāratvena prastutasyābhidhātumucitatvāt /
tasmād yathoktameva sādhu /
children.translated_text: Here, in the <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) of the property called 'bewilderment from fear' attributed to the earth, the cause — trembling, etc. — is stated. When [the cause is] not stated, as in 'The darkness smears, as it were, the limbs,' etc. Here, in the <s>utprekṣā</s> of agency of the action of smearing attributed to darkness, the cause — pervading, etc. — is implied. But when pervading etc. is the object of the <s>utprekṣā</s>, another cause would have to be sought. And it is not proper for the object [of fancy] itself to be implied, since the subject is suitable for being expressed as the substratum of the fancied [quality]. Therefore, what has been stated is correct.

children.text:
phalotprekṣāyāṃ yadeva tasya kāraṇaṃ tadeva nimittam /
tasyānupādāne kasya tatphalatvenoktaṃ syāt /
tasmāttatra tasya nimittasyopādānameva na prakārāntaram /

children.translated_text: For example—
'For the purpose of exchanging ancient horses
stationed on chariots, [the sun] set forth toward the northern direction, the birthplace of swift steeds.'

In <s>phalotprekṣā</s> (fancy about the result), that which is the cause of the [fancied] result is itself the basis (<s>nimitta</s>). When it is not stated, what could be said to have that as its result? Therefore, in such cases, the statement of the basis is the only [possibility], not any other mode.
Here, the exchange of horses — the fancied result — has its cause, namely the journey northward, stated as the basis.

children.text:
tadasāvutprekṣāyāḥ kakṣyāvibhāgaḥ pracuratayā sthito 'pi lakṣye duravadhāratvādiha na prapañcitaḥ /
tasyāścevādiśabdavanmanyeśabdo 'pi pratipādakaḥ /
kiṃ tūtprekṣāsāmagrathabhāve manyeśabdaprayogo vitarkameva pratipādayati /
yathodāhṛtaṃ prāk 'ahaṃ tvinduṃ manye tvadariviraha' ityādi /
children.translated_text: Thus, this classification of <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), although extensively established, is not elaborated here because it is difficult to discern in actual examples. And for this [figure], like the word '<s>iva</s>' (as if), the word '<s>manye</s>' (I think) too is an indicator. However, in the absence of the complete apparatus of <s>utprekṣā</s>, the use of the word '<s>manye</s>' indicates only <s>vitarka</s> (conjecture). As was previously exemplified: 'But I think — the separation from your enemy,' etc.
<s>Sūtra</s> 23:

Having thus determined <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) when the <s>adhyavasāya</s> (determination) is in the process of being established, he now defines <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) when it is [already] established—
When the determined (<s>adhyavasita</s>) is predominant, it is <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole). [RuAss 23]

children.text:
adhyavasāne trayaṃ saṃbhavati- svarūpaṃ viṣayo viṣayī ca /
viṣayasya hi viṣayiṇāntarnigīrṇatve 'dhyavasāyasya svarūpotthānam /
tatra sādhyatve svarūpaprādhānyam /
siddhatve tvadhyavamitaprādhānyam /
viṣayaprādhānyamadhyavasāye naiva saṃbhavati /
adhyavasitaprādhānye cātiśayoktiḥ /
anyāśca pañcaprakārāḥ /
bhede 'bhedaḥ /
abhede bhedaḥ /
saṃbandhe 'saṃbandhaḥ /
asaṃbandhe saṃbandhaḥ /
kāryakāraṇapaurvāparyavidhvaṃsaśca /
children.translated_text: In <s>adhyavasāya</s> (determination/superimposition), three elements are possible: the essential nature (<s>svarūpa</s>), the object (<s>viṣaya</s>), and the subject (<s>viṣayin</s>). For when the object is absorbed within the subject, the essential nature of the determination arises. When it is in the process of being established (<s>sādhya</s>), the predominance is of the essential nature. When it is [already] established (<s>siddha</s>), the predominance is of the determined. The predominance of the object is not possible in determination, since [the object] is absorbed. When the determined is predominant, it is <s>atiśayokti</s>. And there are five other varieties: non-difference in difference (<s>bhede 'bheda</s>); difference in non-difference (<s>abhede bheda</s>); non-relation in [actual] relation (<s>saṃbandhe 'saṃbandha</s>); relation in [actual] non-relation (<s>asaṃbandhe saṃbandha</s>); and destruction of the temporal sequence of cause and effect (<s>kāryakāraṇapaurvāparyavidhvaṃsa</s>).
Among these, non-difference in difference, for example—
'The lotus is in the water, and in the lotus there are water-lilies, and those are upon a golden creeper;
and she is delicate and charming — what is this cascade of wonders!'
Here, in the [actual] difference between the face etc. and the lotus etc., non-difference [is asserted].
Difference in non-difference, for example—
'Other is the grace, and other too is some particular manner of conduct;
O dark one, O <s>Prajāpati</s> of ordinary women, your outline cannot possibly exist [in them].'
('Other is the charm, and other too is some particular way of conduct;
O dark one, O creator of ordinary women, your outline cannot possibly exist.')
Here, even in the non-difference of charm etc. [between the beloved and other women], difference is [asserted] by stating 'other.'

children.text: yathā vā-- 'maggialaddhaṃmi valāmoḍiacuṃbieṃ apyaṇā a uvaṇamie /
children.translated_text: Or, for example— 'When obtained by chance, when kissed by force, when brought by oneself, and when offered [by the beloved],
in a single lip of the beloved, different different flavors of <s>rasa</s> arise.'
('When obtained on the road, when kissed by force, when brought by oneself, and when offered,
in a single lip of the beloved, different different varieties of <s>rasa</s> (flavor) arise.')
Non-relation in [actual] relation, for example—

children.text: 'lāvaṇyadraviṇavyayo na gaṇitaḥ kleśo mahānsvīkṛtaḥ svacchandaṃ carato janasya hṛdaye cintājvaro nirmitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The expenditure of the wealth of beauty was not reckoned; great suffering was undertaken; in the heart of the freely roaming people, a fever of anxiety was created.

children.text: eṣāpi svaguṇānurūparamaṇābhāvād varākī hatā ko 'rthaścetasi vedhasā vinihitastanvyāstanuṃ tanvatā' //
children.translated_text: Even she, poor thing, is ruined because there is no lover worthy of her own qualities — what purpose was intended by the Creator (<s>Vidhi</s>) when he fashioned the body of that slender one!'
Here, even of the undifferentiated <s>rasa</s> (flavor) of the beloved's lip, there is a suggestion of difference through the division of circumstances.
Here, even though there is [an actual] relation of expenditure with the wealth of beauty, non-relation is presented for the purpose of conveying the extreme degree of the slender one's beauty.

children.text: yathā vā-- 'asyāḥ sargavidhau prajāpatipabhūccandro nu kāntipradaḥ śṛṅgāraikarasaḥ svayaṃ nu madano māso nu puṣkākaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Or, for example— 'In creating her, was <s>Prajāpati</s> the Moon, a bestower of radiance? Was <s>Madana</s> (Cupid) himself the sole <s>rasa</s> of <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment)? Was the month of <s>Puṣpa</s> (spring) [the cause]?

children.text: vedābhyāsajaḍaḥ kathaṃ nu viṣayavyāvṛttakautūhalo nirmātuṃ prabhavenmanoharamidaṃ rūpaṃ purāṇo muniḥ' //
children.translated_text: How could that ancient sage, dull from the study of the <s>Vedas</s>, whose curiosity has turned away from sense objects, be capable of creating this captivating form?'
Relation in [actual] non-relation, for example—
'If a flower were placed upon a coral shoot, or if a pearl were set upon a bright coral—
then it might imitate the radiance of that clear smile of hers, adorned with the glow of copper-red lips.'
Here, even though there is [an actual] relation with the creation by the ancient <s>Prajāpati</s>, non-relation is stated.

children.text: atra saṃbhāvanayā saṃbandhaḥ yathā vā- 'dāho 'mbhaḥprasṛtiṃpacaḥ pracayavān bāṣpaḥ praṇālocitaḥ śvāsāḥ preṅkhikatadīpradīpakalikāḥ pāṇṭimni magnaṃ vapuḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, there is [asserted] relation through supposition. Or, for example— 'A burning [like fire], a flow of water, a copious swelling of tears, a breath examined — sighs [like] the flickering of a lamp fed by them, the body sunk in pallor;

children.text: kiṃ tāmyatkathagrāmi rātrimakhilāṃ tvanmārgavātāgrane hastacchattraniruddhacandramahasastasyāḥ sthitirvartate' //
children.translated_text: what is she suffering, what is the story? Throughout the entire night, before the draft on the path to you, she stands like one holding an umbrella that obscures the moonlight.'
Here, even in the [actual] non-relation between burning etc. and the flow of water etc., relation is stated as established.
Reversal, for example—
'First the heart was struck by the flower-arrow of <s>Mālatī</s> (jasmine);
only later, O beloved of the beautiful one, did you come within the range of her eyes.'
Destruction of the temporal sequence of cause and effect is either through reversal of temporal order or through simultaneity.
Simultaneity, for example—
'Dense, trembling clouds; the forest breeze fragrant with <s>kuṭaja</s>, <s>arjuna</s>, and <s>nīpa</s> trees—
this season has arrived; alas, the wives of travelers are carried away!'

children.text:
eṣu pañcasu bhedeṣu bhede 'bhedādivacanaṃ lokātikrāntagocaram /
ataścātrātiśayākhyaṃ yatphalaṃ prayojakatvānnimittaṃ tatrābhedādhyavasāyaḥ /
tathā hi 'kamalamanambhasi' ityādau vadanādīnāṃ kamalādyairbhede 'pi vāstavaṃ saundaryaṃ kavisamarpitena saundaryeṇābhedenādhyavasitaṃ bhede 'bhedavacanasya nimittam /
tatra ca siddho 'dhyavasāya ityadhyavasitaprādhānyam /
na tu vadanādīnāṃ kamalādibhirabhedādhyavasāyo yojanīyaḥ, abhede bheda ityādiṣu prakāreṣvaṣyāpteḥ /
tatra hi 'aṇṇaṃ laḍahṛttaṇaaṃ' ityādau sātiśayaṃ laḍahatvaṃ nimittabhūtabhedenādhyavasitam /
evamanyatrāpi jñeyam /
tadabhiprāyeṇaivādhyavasitaprādhānyam /
prakārapañcakamadhyātkāryakāraṇabhāvena yaḥ prakāraḥ sa kāryakāraṇatāśrayālaṅkāraprastāve prapañcārthaṃ lakṣiyiṣyate /
children.translated_text: In these five varieties, the statement of non-difference in difference, etc., pertains to what transcends ordinary [experience]. Therefore, here the result called 'excess' (<s>atiśaya</s>), being the motivating factor, is the cause, and the <s>adhyavasāya</s> (determination) of non-difference serves as such. Thus, in 'The lotus is in the water' etc., even though there is [actual] difference between the face etc. and the lotus etc., the natural beauty is determined through non-difference with the beauty bestowed by the poet — and the statement of non-difference in difference serves as the cause. And there the determination is established, hence the predominance of the determined. But the determination of non-difference between the face etc. and the lotus etc. should not be construed [differently], since it would also apply in the varieties such as 'difference in non-difference' etc. For there, in 'Other is the charm' etc., the excessive charm is determined through the difference that serves as the cause. The same should be understood in other cases as well. With this purport, the predominance of the determined [is stated]. Among the five varieties, that variety which involves cause-and-effect relation will be further elaborated in the context of the ornament based on causation.
<s>Sūtra</s> 24:

children.text:
evamadhyavasāyāśrayamalaṅkāradvayamuktvā gamyamānaupamyāśrayā alaṅkārā idānīmucyante /
tatrāpi padārthavākyārtagatatvena teṣāṃ dvaividhye padārthagatamalaṅkāradvayaṃ krameṇocyate-
children.translated_text: Having thus stated two ornaments based on <s>adhyavasāya</s> (determination), ornaments based on implied similarity (<s>gamyamāna aupamya</s>) are now stated. Here too, since they are of two kinds — pertaining to word-meaning (<s>padārtha</s>) and sentence-meaning (<s>vākyārtha</s>) — the two ornaments pertaining to word-meaning are stated in order—

children.text: aupamyasya gamyatve padārthagatatvena prastutānāmaprastutānāṃ vā samānadharmābhisaṃbandhe tulyayogitā || 24 ||
children.translated_text: When similarity is implied, and when there is a connection of common properties among things that are contextual (<s>prastuta</s>) or non-contextual (<s>aprastuta</s>) at the level of word-meaning, [the figure is] <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal application). [RuAss 24]

children.text:
ivādyaprayoge hyaupanyasya gamyatvam /
tatra prākaraṇikānāmapraraṇikānāṃ vārthānāṃ samānaguṇakriyāsaṃbandhe anvitārthā tulyayogitā /

children.translated_text: For example—
'Adorned with borders of newly-sprouted leaves, displaying full pinkness,
the blossoming [faces/lotuses], through the power of the sun's rays — both the days and the lotuses increased in glory.'

When particles like '<s>iva</s>' (like) are not used, similarity is implied. Therein, when contextual or non-contextual things are connected through common qualities or actions as construed meaning, it is <s>tulyayogitā</s>.

children.text:
atra ṛtuvarṇanasya prakāntatvāddinānāṃ padmānāṃ ca prakṛtatvād vṛddhigamanaṃ kriyā /
evaṃ guṇe 'pi /

children.translated_text: For example—
'The <s>yogapaṭṭa</s> (yoga-belt), the mass of matted hair, the tree-bark, the deer-skin—
if these are fitting for your limbs, let it be said so.'
Here, since the description of the season is the context, both the days and the lotuses are contextual, and their increase in glory is the action. Similarly with respect to quality.
When [the things] are non-contextual, for example—
'The dust fallen from your horse-army runs upon the face of him,

children.text: bhagnasya gūrjaranṛpasya rajaḥ kayāpi tanvyā tavāsilatayā ca yaśaḥ prabhṛṣṭam' //
children.translated_text: the defeated <s>Gūrjara</s> king — wiped away by some slender woman, and your fame [is wiped] by the edge of [your] sword.'
Fitness is the quality.

children.text: atra gūrjaraṃ prati nāyikāsilatayoraprākaraṇikatve mārjanaṃ kriyā /

children.translated_text: With respect to quality, for example—
'Seeing the softness of your limbs, in whose mind does there not arise
the [impression of] hardness of <s>mālatī</s> flowers, moon-crescents, and plantain trees?'
Here, when the heroine and the sword-edge are non-contextual with respect to the <s>Gūrjara</s> [king], the wiping is the action.
Hardness is the quality [shared]. Thus this [figure] has been explained as fourfold.
START Sūtra 25:

Having established <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal conjunction) when the relevant and non-relevant [subjects] are separated, when they are combined, [the figure] called <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination) is stated—
The [figure involving] relevant and non-relevant [subjects together] is <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination). || 25 ||

children.text:
aupamyasya gamyatva ityādyanuvartate /
prākaraṇikāprākaraṇikayormadhyādekatra nirdiṣṭaḥ samāno dharmaḥ prasaṅganānyatropakārāddīpanāddīpasādṛśyena dīpakākhyālaṅkārotthāpakaḥ /
tatrevādyaprayogādupamānopameyabhāvo gamyamānaḥ /
sa ca vāstava eva /
pūrvatra śuddhaprākaraṇikatve śuddhāprākaṇikatvai vā vaivakṣikaḥ, prākaraṇikatvanirvartitatvādupamānopameyabhāvasya /
anekasyaikakriyābhisaṃbandhādaucityātpadārthatvoktiḥ /
vastutastu vākyārthatve ādimadhyāntavākyagatatvena dharmasya vṛttāvādibhamadhyāntadīpakākhyāstrayo 'sya bhedāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The similarity being implied' etc. continues [from the previous sūtra]. A common property, stated in one of the two—the contextual and the non-contextual—illuminates the other through incidental connection, and like a lamp (<s>dīpa</s>) generates the figure called <s>dīpaka</s>. And from the initial usage itself, the relation of <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) and <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison) is implied. That relation is indeed real. In the previous case [<s>tulyayogitā</s>], when [both are] purely contextual or purely non-contextual, [the relation is] intended; since the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relation is produced through contextuality. Due to the connection of many [subjects] with a single action, the expression in terms of word-meanings is appropriate. But in reality, when [the common property] belongs to the sentence-meaning in a pair of sentences, the property being in the beginning, middle, or end of the sentence gives rise to three varieties called beginning-, middle-, and end-<s>dīpaka</s>.

children.text: krameṇodāharaṇam - 'rehai mihireṇa ṇahaṃ raseṇa kavvaṃ sareṇa jovvaṇaaṃ /
children.translated_text: Examples in order— [Prakrit:] 'The sky shines with the sun, poetry with <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), youth with love,
the course of the river with nectar, [and] this world with you, O lord of men.'

children.text: ('reyate mihireṇa nabho rasena kāvyaṃ sareṇa [smareṇa] yauvanam amṛtena dhunīdhavaḥsvayā naramātha! bhuvanamidam' //)//
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] 'The sky shines with the sun, poetry with <s>rasa</s>, youth with love (<s>smara</s>), the river's course with nectar, and this world with you, O lord of men.'
'Having purified the regions of the sky by her passage, at the day's end, to go to her abode,

children.text: pracakrame pallavarāgatāmrā prabhā pataṅgasya munaśca dhenuḥ' //
children.translated_text: the radiance of the sun, coppery-red like fresh sprouts, set forth—and so did the sage's cow.'
[Prakrit:] 'The wealth of misers, the crest-gems of serpents, the manes of lions,
the breasts of well-born maidens—from where can they be touched by the dead?'
[Sanskrit rendering:] 'The wealth of misers, the crest-gems of serpents, the manes of lions,
the breasts of well-born maidens—how can the dead touch [any of] these?'

children.text:
evamekakriyaṃ dīpakatrayaṃ nirṇītam /
atra ca yathānekakārakagatatvennaikakriyā dīpakaṃ tathānekakriyāgatatvenaikakārakamapi dīpakam /

children.translated_text: As follows—
'To help the good, to bear <s>Lakṣmī</s> (fortune), to travel through the sky,

children.text: na kutūhali kasya manaścaritaṃ ca mahātmanāṃ śrotum' //
children.translated_text: whose mind is not eager [to do these]?—and also to hear the deeds of great souls.'

Thus the three types of <s>dīpaka</s> with a single action have been determined. And here, just as <s>dīpaka</s> involves a single action relating to multiple case-relations, so too a single case-relation involving multiple actions is also <s>dīpaka</s>.

children.text:
atropakaraṇādyanekakriyākartṛtvena kutūhalaviśiṣṭaṃ mano nirdiṣṭam /
chāyānrareṇa tu mālādīpakaṃ prastāvāntare lakṣyayiṣyate /
children.translated_text: Here, the mind, qualified by eagerness, is stated as the agent of multiple actions such as helping etc. The garland-<s>dīpaka</s> (<s>mālā-dīpaka</s>), however, will be illustrated on another occasion.
START Sūtra 26:
When the common property, belonging to the sentence-meaning, is stated separately in a pair of sentences, [the figure is] <s>prativastūpamā</s> (counter-subject simile). || 26 ||

children.text:
padārthārabdho vākyārtha iti padārthagatālaṅkārānantaraṃ vākyārthagatālaṅkāraprastāvaḥ /
tatra sāmānyadharmasyevādyupādāne sakṛnnirdeśe upamā /
vastuprativastubhāvenāsakṛnnirdeśe 'pi saiva /
ivādyanupādāne sakṛnnirdeśe upamā /
vastuprativastubhāvenāsakṛnnirdeśe tu śuddhasāmānyarūpatvaṃ bimbapratibimbabhāvo vā /
ādyaḥ prakāraḥ prativastūpamā /
vastu-śabdasya vākyārthavācitve prativāvākyārthamupamā sāmyamityanvarthāśrayaṇāt /
kevalaṃ kāvyasamayātparyāyāntareṇa pṛthaṅnirdeśaḥ /
dvitīyaprakārāśrayeṇa dṛṣṭānto vakṣyate /
tadevamaupamyāśrayeṇaiva prativastūpamā /

children.translated_text: As follows—
'The <s>cakora</s> birds alone are skilled in the art of drinking moonlight;
the women of <s>Āvantī</s> alone are expert in the sport of love.'

Since sentence-meaning arises from word-meanings, after the figures belonging to word-meaning, [now comes] the occasion for figures belonging to sentence-meaning. There, when the common property is initially presented with the particle 'iva' etc. and stated once, it is <s>upamā</s> (simile). When stated repeatedly through the relation of subject and counter-subject, it is still the same [simile]. When without 'iva' etc. and stated once, it is <s>upamā</s>. But when stated repeatedly through the relation of subject and counter-subject, it is either of the nature of a pure commonality, or a reflection-image (<s>bimba-pratibimba</s>) relation. The first type is <s>prativastūpamā</s>. Since the word 'vastu' means 'sentence-meaning,' <s>prativastūpamā</s> means 'simile of each sentence-meaning'—following the literal sense. The only distinction is that, by poetic convention, [the common property] is stated separately through different terms. The second type will be discussed as <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example). Thus <s>prativastūpamā</s> is based precisely on the similarity relation.

children.text:
atra caturatvaṃ sādhāraṇe dharmaṃ upamānavākye, upameyavākye tu nipuṇapadena nirdiṣṭaḥ /
na kevasamiyaṃ sādharmyeṇa yāvad vaidharmyeṇāpi /
yathātraivottarasthāne 'vināvantīrna nipuṇāḥ sudṛśo ratanarmaṇi' iti pāṭhe /
children.translated_text: Here, the common property of 'skillfulness' is stated in the <s>upamāna</s> (standard) sentence with the word 'clever,' and in the <s>upameya</s> (subject) sentence with the word 'expert.' Moreover, this [figure] applies not only through similarity but also through dissimilarity. As here itself, in the alternative reading: 'Without the women of <s>Āvantī</s>, none are expert in the sport of love.'
When that very [common property] is stated in the manner of image and reflection, [the figure is] <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example). || 27 ||
START Sūtra 27:

children.text:
taṣṇāpīti na kevalamupamānopameyayoḥ /
tacchabdena sāmānyadharmaḥ pratyavamṛṣṭaḥ /
ayamapi sādharmyavaidharmyābhyāṃ dvividhaḥ /

children.translated_text: The first, as follows—

children.text: 'abdhirlaṅghita eva vānarabhaṭaiḥ kiṃ tvasya gambhīratā- , māpātālanimagnapīvaratanurjānāti manthācalaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The ocean was indeed crossed by the monkey-soldiers—but its depth is known only to Mount <s>Manthara</s> (the churning mountain) whose massive body was submerged to the netherworld.

children.text: devīṃ vācamupāsate hi bahyavaḥ sāraṃ tu sārastvataṃ jānīte nitarāmasau gurukulakliṣṭo murāriḥ kaviḥ' //
children.translated_text: Many worship the goddess of speech (<s>Vāc</s>), but the essence is known only to that <s>Murāri</s> (enemy of <s>Mura</s>, i.e., <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>)-poet, thoroughly trained in the teacher's school.'
'That very' means not merely of the <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s>. By the word 'that,' the common property is recalled. This too is twofold, through similarity and dissimilarity.

children.text:
atra yadyapi ñcānākhya eko dharmo nirdiṣṭastathāpi na tannibandhanamaupabhyaṃ vivakṣitam /
yannibandhanaṃ ca vivakṣitaṃ tatrābdhilaṅghanādāvastyeva divyavāgupāsanādinā pratibimbanam /

children.translated_text: The second, as follows—

children.text: 'kṛtaṃ ca garvābhimukhaṃ manastvayā kimanyadevaṃ nihatāśca no 'rayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Your mind has turned toward pride—what else? [But] our enemies have been slain.
For the darkness endures only so long as the radiant sun has not reached the summit of the eastern mountain.'

Here, although a single common property called 'knowing' is stated, the intended similarity is not based on that. Rather, in the basis of what is intended, there is indeed a reflection from the crossing of the ocean through divine worship of speech, etc.
Here, the reflection is through dissimilarity—the slain state [of enemies] contrasted with the abiding [of darkness], etc.
START Sūtra 28:

children.text: saṃbhāvatāsaṃbhavatā vā vastusaṃbandhena gamyamānaṃ pratibimbakaraṇaṃ nidarśanā || 28 ||
children.translated_text: When the reflection-making is apprehended through a connection with a thing that is possible or impossible, [the figure is] <s>nidarśanā</s> (illustration). || 28 ||

children.text:
pratibimbakaraṇaprastāvenāsyā lakṣaṇam /
tatra kkacitsaṃbhavanneva vastusaṃbandhaḥ svasāmarthyāddhimbapratibimbabhāvaṃ kalpayati /
kvacitpunaranvayabādhādasaṃbhāvatā vastusaṃbandhena pratibimbanamākṣipyate /

children.translated_text: An example with a possible thing-connection—
'He who places the sun-god, arrived [at his head], in the position of a crest-jewel,
thereby instructing the householders that the duty of the good is to honor guests.'

Its definition is given in the context of the discussion of reflection-making. There, sometimes a connection with a thing that is indeed possible, by its own capacity, creates the image-reflection relation. Sometimes, however, due to the obstruction of logical connection, the impossibility of the thing-connection draws forth the reflection.
An example with an impossible thing-connection—
'The moon, naturally crooked [in the form of a crescent], whose two tips are licked by the rays of the great serpent-king's jewel bound in the matted locks,
approaches you, O <s>Yamya</s> (the southern one), touching the play of the strung bow of the god of love.'
Here, 'instructing' in the causative (ṇic) is used in the sense of performing the corresponding action—so the thing-connection is possible.

Here, the touching by the moon—which is another entity—of the play belonging to the bow of the god of love is impossible; [yet] it conveys a play resembling that play—from the great distance [of the impossible connection], the creation of a reflection is stated.
The sentence-meaning application, as follows—
'That the lac-dye is removed from the gems of your toenails—
this is the whitening of the moon by sandal-paste anointing.'
This [<s>nidarśanā</s>] is also twofold, according to the distinction of word-meaning and sentence-meaning application. The word-meaning application has just been illustrated.

children.text:
kecittu dṛṣṭāntālaṅkāro 'yamityāhustadasat /
nirapekṣayorvākyārthayorhi bimbapratibimbabhāvo dṛṣṭāntaḥ /
yatra ca prakṛte vākyārthe vākyārthāntaramāropyate sāmānādhikaraṇyena tatra saṃbandhānupapattimūlā nidarśanaiva yuktā, na dṛṣṭāntaḥ /

children.translated_text: And thus—
'If this form, difficult to find even in the women's quarters, belongs to a forest-dweller,
then surely the garden creepers have been put to shame by the forest creepers through their virtues.'

Some say this is the figure of <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example), but that is incorrect. For <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> is the image-reflection relation of two independent sentence-meanings. But where one sentence-meaning is superimposed upon the primary sentence-meaning in co-reference, there, due to the impossibility of [real] connection, <s>nidarśanā</s> alone is appropriate, not <s>dṛṣṭānta</s>.
Here, the cognition of <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> should not be produced, since by the stated principle, the apprehension of <s>nidarśanā</s> [is correct].

children.text: iyaṃ copemeya upamānavṛttasyāsaṃbhavātpratipāditā pūrvaiḥ vastutastūpameyavṛttasyopamāne 'saṃbhavādapi bhavati /
children.translated_text: This [<s>nidarśanā</s>] has been established by the earlier authorities [as occurring] when the activity of the <s>upamāna</s> is impossible in the <s>upameya</s>; but in reality, it also occurs when the activity of the <s>upameya</s> is impossible in the <s>upamāna</s>,
since the disruption of connection exists in both cases.
As follows— 'That pallor of the cheeks of the women of <s>Gauḍa</s> in separation—
it was perceived in the pollen within the clusters of date-palm flowers.'

children.text:
atra gaṇḍatalaṃ prakṛtam /
taddharmasya pāṇḍimnaḥ kharjūrīreṇuṣvasaṃbhavādaupamyapratītiḥ /
eṣa ca prakāraḥ śṛṅkhalānyāyenāpi bhavati /
yathā-
'muṇḍasire boraphalaṃ borovari boraaṃ thiraṃ dharasi /
viggucchāai appā ṇāliacheā chalijjanti' /
children.translated_text: Here, the cheeks are the primary subject. The impossibility of the cheek's property, pallor, [being found] in the date-palm pollen [creates] the apprehension of similarity. And this type also occurs in chain-fashion (<s>śṛṅkhalā-nyāya</s>). As follows— [Prakrit verse:] 'On the shaven head a <s>bora</s>-fruit, on the <s>bora</s>-fruit the firmness of a <s>bora</s> [berry] you bear; self-repulsed, the coconut-pieces fall away.'
As follows—
'Weeping in the wilderness is done, a corpse's body is anointed, a lotus is planted on dry land, rain is poured upon a desert for a long time,

children.text: śvapucchamavanāmitaṃ badhirakarṇajāpaḥ kṛtaḥ dhṛto 'ndhamukhadarpaṇo yadabudho janaḥ sevitaḥ' //
children.translated_text: a dog's tail is straightened, a whisper is made in a deaf ear, a mirror is held before a blind face—[all this is what happens] when a foolish person is served.'
This is also sometimes seen occurring in a garland (<s>mālā</s>) fashion.
As follows—

children.text: 'utkope tvayi kiñcideva calati drāggūrjarakṣmābhṛtā muktā bhūrna paraṃ bhayānmarujuṣāṃ yāvattadeṇīdṛśām /
children.translated_text: 'When you are even slightly angered, the king of <s>Gūrjara</s> instantly abandons the earth—not more through fear; whereas [with those] doe-eyed women,

children.text: padbhyāṃ haṃsagatirmukhena śaśinaḥ kāntiḥ kucābhyāmapi kṣāmābhyāṃ sahasaiva vanyakariṇāṃ gaṇḍasthalīvibhramaḥ' //
children.translated_text: from their feet comes the gait of swans, from their face the beauty of the moon, and from their slender breasts comes suddenly the splendor of the temple-mounds of wild elephants.'
Sometimes, however, due to the force of negation, the apprehension [of the figure] is drawn forth, and it occurs even with the impossibility of connection.

children.text:
atra muktena niṣedhapadaṃ tadanyathānupapattyā pādayorhasagatiprātpirākṣipyate /
sā ca tayoranupapannā sādṛśyaṃ gamayatīti asaṃbhavadvastusaṃbanvanibandhanā nidarśanā /
children.translated_text: Here, by the word 'mukta' (freed), the negative word is implied, and through the impossibility of any other interpretation, the attainment of swan-like gait at the feet is suggested. And that, being impossible for those two, conveys similarity — thus it is <s>nidarśanā</s> (illustration) based on the connection with an impossible state of affairs.
[Sūtra 29:]

When difference is predominant, and the subject of comparison (<s>upameya</s>) is superior to the standard of comparison (<s>upamāna</s>), or the reverse, [the figure is] <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast). // RuAss 29 //

children.text:
adhunā bhedaprādhānyenālaṅkārakathanam /
bhedo vailakṣaṇyam /
sa ca dvidhā bhavati, upamānādupameyasyādhikaguṇatve viparyaye vā bhāvāt /
viparyayo nyūnaguṇatvam /
children.translated_text: Now, the discussion of figures of speech through the predominance of difference. Difference means dissimilarity. And it is twofold, since it occurs when the subject of comparison has superior qualities to the standard of comparison, or the reverse. The reverse means having inferior qualities.
Examples in order: 'Desiring to see the charming play of the eyelash-creepers of your thousand eyes,
the swarms of bees do not delight in the pools where blue-lotus beds are eager to bloom.'

children.text: 'kṣīṇaḥ kṣoṇo 'pi śaśī bhūyo bhūyo vivardhate satyam /
children.translated_text: 'Though waned and diminished, the moon truly waxes again and again;

children.text: virama prasīda sundari yauvanamanivarti yātaṃ tu' //
children.translated_text: cease, be at peace, O beautiful one — but youth, once gone, does not return.'

children.text:
atra vikasvaranīlotpalinyapekṣayā akṣisahasrasya pakṣmalatayā adhikaguṇatvam /
candrāpekṣayā ca yauvanasya nyūnaguṇatvam /
śaśivailakṣaṇyena tasyāpunarāgamāt /
children.translated_text: Here, compared to the blooming blue-lotus bed, the thousand eyes with their eyelash-creepers have superior quality. And compared to the moon, youth has inferior quality — because of its dissimilarity from the moon, namely its not returning again.
[Sūtra 30:]

When one of the standard or subject of comparison is indicated as primary, and the other is connected in the sense of accompaniment, [the figure is] <s>sahokti</s> (concurrent expression). // RuAss 30 //

children.text:
bhedaprādhānya ityeva /
guṇaprādhānabhāvanimittakamatra bhedaprādhānyam /
sahārthaprayuktaśca guṇaprādhānabhāvaḥ /
upamānopameyatvaṃ cātra vaivakṣikam, dvayorapi prākaraṇikatvādaprākaraṇikaraṇikatvādvā /
sahārthasāmarthyāddhi tayoḥ tulyakakṣatvam /
tatra tṛtīyāntasya niyamena guṇatvādupamānatvam /
arthācca pariśiṣṭasya pradhānatvādupameyatvam /
śabdaścātra guṇaprādhānabhāvaḥ /
vastutastu viparyayo 'pi syāt /
tatra niyamenātiśayoktimūlatvamasyāḥ /
sā ca kāryakāraṇapratiniyamaviparyayarūpā abhedādhyavasāyarūpā ca /
abhedādhyavasāyaśca śleṣabhittiko 'nyathā vā /
sāhityaṃ cātra katrādinānābhedaṃ jñeyam /
tatra ca -
'kāryakāraṇapratiniyamaviparyayarūpā yathā -
'bhavadaparādhaiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃtāpo vardhatetarāmasyāḥ' /
atrāparādhānāṃ saṃtāpaṃ prati hetutve 'pi tulyakālatvenopanibandhaḥ /

children.translated_text: The form of determination of non-difference based on <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning) is as follows:
'The sun has gone to setting; together with the enemies, let the armies be withdrawn.'
Here, 'going to setting' has double meaning,
because the word 'astam' has both meanings [setting of the sun and destruction].

This is indeed [within the context of] predominance of difference. The predominance of difference here is caused by the distinction between primary and secondary. And the distinction of primary and secondary is effected by the sense of accompaniment (<s>saha-artha</s>). The status of standard and subject of comparison here is determined by intention, since either can be contextually relevant or irrelevant. For by the force of the sense of accompaniment, the two are on equal footing. There, the one in the instrumental case, being invariably the secondary, is the standard of comparison. And by implication, the remaining one, being primary, is the subject of comparison. Here the distinction of primary and secondary is verbal. But in substance, the reverse may also occur. There, this [figure] is invariably rooted in <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole). And that is of the form of reversal of the fixed cause-effect relationship, and of the form of determination of non-difference. The determination of non-difference is either based on <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning) or otherwise. And accompaniment here should be known as having various forms through agent, etc. In that, the form of reversal of the fixed cause-effect relationship is as follows: 'Together with your offenses, the anguish of this lady increases greatly.' Here, although the offenses are causes of the anguish, they are joined as if simultaneous.

children.text:
tadanyathārūpā yathā -
'kumudavanaiḥ saha saṃprati vighaṭante cakravākamithunāni' /
atra vighaṭanaṃ saṃbandhibhedādbhinnaṃ na tu śliṣṭam /
etadviśeṣaparihāreṇa sahoktimātraṃ nālaṅkāraḥ /
yathā-

children.translated_text: 'Let me sport with him on the shores of the ocean, in the rustling groves of palm trees' — in such cases [there is no figure].
These very [examples] are illustrations of accompaniment in the agent.

children.text: karmasāhitye yathā - 'dyujano mutyunā sārdhaṃ yasyājau tārakāmaye /
children.translated_text: In accompaniment in the object, as follows: 'In whose battle called <s>Tārakāmaya</s>, the gods together with Death
fulfilled wishes beyond expectation through a servant called <s>Cakra</s> (discus).'

The other form [not based on double meaning] is as follows: 'Together with the water-lily groves, the <s>cakravāka</s> couples now separate.' Here, 'separation' is differentiated by the difference in the related objects, not through double meaning. Without these specific distinctions, mere concurrent expression is not a figure of speech. As follows:

children.text:
atra karotikriyāpekṣayā dyujanasya mṛtyośca karmatvam /
eṣā ca māsayāpi bhavantī dṛśyate /

children.translated_text: As follows:

children.text: 'utkṣitpaṃ saha kauśikasya pulakaiḥ sārdhaṃ mukhairnāmitaṃ bhūpānāṃ janakasya saṃśayadhiyā sākaṃ samāsphālitam /
children.translated_text: 'It was lifted together with the goose-bumps of <s>Kauśika</s> (Viśvāmitra), bent together with the faces of the kings, struck together with the doubt-filled mind of <s>Janaka</s>,

children.text: vaidehyā manasā samaṃ ca sahasākṛṣṭaṃ tato bhārgava- prauḍhāhaṅkṛtikandalena ca samaṃ tad bhagnamaiśaṃ dhanuḥ' //
children.translated_text: suddenly drawn together with the heart of <s>Vaidehī</s> (Sītā), and then broken together with the bursting forth of the proud arrogance of <s>Bhārgava</s> (Paraśurāma) — that bow of <s>Īśa</s> (Śiva).'
Here, with respect to the action of 'making,' the gods and Death are in the object case. And this is also seen occurring with combination.
[Sūtra 31:]
He now defines <s>vinokti</s> (expression of absence), which is the counterpart of <s>sahokti</s>:
When, without something, there is the absence of another's existence or non-existence, [the figure is] <s>vinokti</s> (expression of absence). // RuAss 31 //

children.text:
sattvasya śobhanatvasyābhāvo 'śobhanatvam /
evamasattvasyāśobhanatvasyābhāvaḥ śobhanatvam /
tedve sattvāsattve yatra kasyacidasaṃnidhānānnibadhyete sā dvidhā vinoktiḥ /
atra ca śobhanatvāśobhanatvasattāsattāyāmeva vaktavyāyāmasattāmukhenābhidhānamanyanivṛttiprayuktā tannivṛttiriti khyāpanārtham /
evaṃ cānyānivṛttau vidhireva prakāśito bhavati /

children.translated_text: The first, as follows:

children.text: 'vinayena vinā kā śrīḥ kā niśā śaśinā vinā /
children.translated_text: 'What is beauty without modesty? What is the night without the moon?
What sort of eloquence is there devoid of true poetic skill?'

The absence of existence, i.e., excellence, is non-excellence. Similarly, the absence of non-existence, i.e., non-excellence, is excellence. Where these two — existence and non-existence — are established due to the absence of something, that is twofold <s>vinokti</s>. And here, when excellence, non-excellence, existence, or non-existence is to be stated, the expression through negation is for the purpose of proclaiming the cessation of the other, prompted by that cessation. And thus, in the non-cessation of the other, a positive injunction alone is illuminated.

children.text: atra vināśabdamantareṇāpi vinārthavivakṣā yathākathañcinnimittībhavati yathā sahoktau sahārthavivakṣā /

children.translated_text: And thus:

children.text: 'nirarthakaṃ janma gataṃ nalinyā yathā na dṛṣṭaṃ tuhināṃśubimbam /
children.translated_text: 'The birth of the water-lily has gone in vain, since it did not see the orb of the moon;

children.text: utpattirindorapi niṣphalaiva na yena dṛṣṭā nalinī prabuddhā' //
children.translated_text: the arising of the moon too is fruitless, since it did not see the water-lily awakened.'

Here, even without the word 'vinā' (without), the intention of the sense of 'without' becomes the occasion in some way or another, just as in <s>sahokti</s> the intention of the sense of 'with' [does].

children.text:
ityādau vinoktireva /
tuhināṃśudarśanaṃ nalinījanmano 'śobhanatvapratīteḥ /
iyaṃ ca parasparavinoktibhaṅgyā camatkārātiśayakṛt /
yathodāhṛte viṣaye /
children.translated_text: In such cases, it is <s>vinokti</s> alone — because the perception of non-excellence of the water-lily's birth [arises from] not seeing the moon. And this, through the mode of mutual <s>vinokti</s>, creates an excess of wonder, as in the example cited.
The second, as follows:
'Without the doe-eyed one, though bold with the brilliance of wit in diverse affairs,
with intentions beautiful as the moon's radiance — this prince is thus a dear friend.'
Here, the absence of non-excellence is expressed through the mode of introducing excellent attributes. This is the twofold <s>vinokti</s>.
[Sūtra 32:]
Now, two figures of speech are stated, relying on the interruption of modifiers. Of these, first, he states <s>samāsokti</s> (compressed expression) based on the equality of modifiers:
When, due to the similarity of modifiers, something not directly relevant (<s>aprastuta</s>) is implied, [the figure is] <s>samāsokti</s> (compressed expression). // RuAss 32 //

children.text:
iha prastutāprastutānāṃ kvacid vācyatvaṃ kvacid gamyatvamiti dvaividhyam /
vācyatvaṃ ca śleṣanirdeśabhaṅgyā pṛthagupādānena vetyapi dvaividhyam /
etad dvibhedamapi śleṣālaṅkārasya viṣayaḥ /
gumyatvaṃ tu prastutaniṣṭhamaprastutapraśaṃsāviṣayaḥ aprastutaniṇṭhaṃ tu samāsoktiviṣayaḥ /
tatra ca nimittaṃ viśeṣaṇasāmyam /
viśeṣyasyāpi sāmye śleṣaprātpeḥ /
viśeṣaṇasāmyāddhi pratīyamānaprastutaṃ prastutāvacchedakatvena pratīyate /
avacchedakatvaṃ ca vyavahārasamāropaḥ /
rūpasamārope tvavacchāditatvena prakṛtasya tadrūpitvād rūpakameva /
children.translated_text: Here, the relevant and irrelevant [meanings] have a twofold nature: sometimes they are expressed, sometimes implied. Expression too has a twofold nature: either through the mode of indicating <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning), or through separate mention. This twofold [expression] is the domain of the figure <s>śleṣa</s>. But implication, when centered on the relevant, is the domain of <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant). When centered on the irrelevant, it is the domain of <s>samāsokti</s>. And there, the cause is the similarity of modifiers. Since, if the qualified noun too were similar, it would result in <s>śleṣa</s>. For through the similarity of modifiers, the implied relevant meaning is understood as the distinguishing factor of the stated meaning. The distinguishing factor is a superimposition of usage. But in superimposition of form, since the subject takes on that very form by being covered, it is <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) alone.

children.text: tacca viśeṣaṇasāmyaṃ śliṣṭatayā sādhāraṇyenaupamyagarbhatvena ca bhavat tridhā bhavati tatra śliṣṭatayā yathā - 'upoḍharāgeṇa vilolatārakaṃ tathā gṛhītaṃ śaśinā niśāmukham ṣa yathā samastaṃ timirāṃśukaṃ tayā puro 'pi rāgādgalitaṃ na lakṣitam' //
children.translated_text: And that similarity of modifiers, occurring through double meaning, through being common, and through containing comparison, becomes threefold. Through double meaning, as follows: 'The face of the night, seized thus by the moon with rising passion, with trembling stars — so that the whole garment of darkness, though slipped from the front due to passion, was not noticed.'
Here, through the power of the double-meaning modifiers of the night and moon, the behavior of a hero [in a love scene] is understood.
Since the night and moon, without abandoning their own nature, are understood as possessing the quality called 'hero-ness.'

children.text: sādhāraṇyena yathā - 'tanvī manoramā bālā lolākṣī puṣpahāsinī /
children.translated_text: Through being common, as follows: 'Slender, charming, young, with restless eyes, laughing with flowers —
she blossoms, O fortunate one, merely at the sight of you.'

children.text:
atra tanvītyādiviśeṣaṇasāmyāllolākṣyā latāvyavahārapratītiḥ /
tatra ca lataikagāmivikāsākhyadharmasasāropaḥ kāraṇam /
anyathā viśeṣaṇasāmyamātreṇa niyatalatāvyavahārasyāpratīteḥ /
vikāsaśca prakṛte upacarito jñeyaḥ /
evaṃ ca kāryasamārope 'pi jñeyā /
iyaṃ ca samāsoktiḥ pūrvāpekṣayāspaṣṭā /
children.translated_text: Here, through the similarity of modifiers beginning with 'slender' etc., the understanding of the usage relating to a creeper for 'the restless-eyed one' arises. And there, the cause is the superimposition of the quality called 'blossoming' which belongs exclusively to a creeper. Otherwise, by mere similarity of modifiers alone, the definite understanding of creeper-usage would not arise. And 'blossoming' should be understood as metaphorically applied to the subject. Similarly it should be understood in the superimposition of effect. And this <s>samāsokti</s> is less clear compared to the former.
Through containing comparison, as follows:
'Adorned with flowers of teeth-radiance, beautiful with hand-tendrils,
with a paddy-field of hair-tresses, well-dressed, with deer-like eyes —'

children.text:
atra dantaprabhā puṣpāṇīveti suveṣatvavaśādupamāgarbhatvena kṛte samāse paścāddantaprabhāsadṛśaiḥ puṣpaiściteti samāsāntarāśrayaṇena samānaviśeṣaṇamāhātmyāllatāvyavahārapratītiḥ /
atraiva 'parītā hariṇekṣaṇā' iti pāṭhe upamārūpasādhakabāghakābhāvāt saṃkarasamāśrayeṇa kṛte yojane paścāt pūrvavat samāsāntaramahimnā latāpratītijñaṃyā /
rūpakagarbhatvena tu samāsāntarāśrayaṇāt samānaviṣeṣaṇatvaṃ bhavadapi na samāsokteḥ prayojakam /
ekadeśavivartirūpakamukhenaivārthāntarapratītestasyā vaiyarthyāt /
na ca pūrvadarśitopamāsaṃkaraviṣaye eṣa nyāyaḥ /
upamāsaṃkarayorekadeśavivartinorabhāvāt /
taccaikadeśavivartirūpakamaśleṣeṇa śleṣeṇa ca bhavatīti dvividham /

children.translated_text: Without <s>śleṣa</s>, for example:
'Seeing with lightning-eyes, the rain cloud [observed] the face of the woman going to meet her lover at night.

children.text: dhārānipātaiḥ saha kiṃ nu vāntaścandro 'yamitpārtataraṃ rarāsa' //
children.translated_text: Did it vomit this moon along with its showers of rain? — thus it wailed even more pitifully.'

Here, [in the compound] 'tooth-radiance-flowers,' when the compound is formed with an <s>upamā</s> (simile) component due to the beauty of the expression [as 'flowers like tooth-radiance'], and then by resorting to a different compound [analysis] as 'decorated with flowers resembling tooth-radiance,' the cognition of the vine-convention is produced through the glory of the common qualifier (<s>samāna-viśeṣaṇa</s>). In the same [verse], with the reading 'surrounded by doe-eyed ones,' since there is no [independent] element that either proves or obstructs the <s>upamā</s> form, when the construction is made by resorting to the combination [of figures], then as before, through the greatness of the alternative compound, the cognition of the vine should be understood. But through resorting to another compound with a <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) component, even though a common qualifier arises, it does not motivate <s>samāsokti</s>, because the cognition of another meaning [occurs] through the mouth of <s>ekadeśavivartirūpaka</s> (metaphor with partial transformation) alone — making that [<s>samāsokti</s>] purposeless. But this principle does not [apply] in the case of the <s>upamā</s>-combination previously shown, because there is no <s>ekadeśavivartin</s> in [mere] <s>upamā</s> combination. And this <s>ekadeśavivartirūpaka</s> is of two kinds: without <s>śleṣa</s> (double entendre) and with <s>śleṣa</s>.

children.text: atra nirīkṣaṇānuguṇyādvidyunnayanairiti rūpake payodasya draṣṭṛpuruṣanirūpaṇamārtataraṃ rarāsetyatra pratīyamānotprekṣāyā nimittatvaṃ bhajate /

children.translated_text: With <s>śleṣa</s>, for example:
'Producing an elaborate painting at the counting-station of <s>Madana</s> (Cupid), with bee-ink marks placed on the large leaf-decorations,

children.text: kuṭilalipibhiḥ kaṃ kāyasthaṃ na nāma visūtrayan vyadhita virahiprāṇeṣvāyavyayāvadhikaṃ madhuḥ' [śrī. ca. 670] //
children.translated_text: with crooked inscriptions — which <s>kāyastha</s> (scribe/embodied one) has he not made to writhe? Spring has performed the accounts of income and expenditure upon the lives of those separated [from their beloveds]!'

Here, in the <s>rūpaka</s> 'with lightning-eyes' — consistent with the act of seeing — the identification of the rain cloud as a male observer becomes the cause of the <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) perceived in 'wailed even more pitifully.'

children.text:
atra hi pattralipikāyasthaśabdeṣu śleṣagarbhe rūpakaṃ dvirephamaṣīlavairityetadrūpakanimittam /
asya ca pracuraḥ prayogaviṣaya iti na samāsoktibuddhiḥ kāryā /
children.translated_text: Here, in the words 'leaf-decoration,' '<s>kāyastha</s>' (scribe), there is a <s>rūpaka</s> containing <s>śleṣa</s>; and 'with bee-ink marks' is the basis of the <s>rūpaka</s>. And since this [figure] has abundant scope for use, one should not think of it as [merely] <s>samāsokti</s>.

children.text:
tadevaṃ śliṣṭaviśeṣaṇasamutthāpitaikā /
sādhāraṇaviśeṣaṇasamutthāpitā tu dharmakāryasamāropābhyāṃ dvibhedā /
aupamyagarbhaviśeṣaṇasamutthāpitopamāsaṃkarasamāsābhyāṃ dvibhedā /
rūpakasamāśrayeṇa tu bhedadvayamasyā na viṣayaḥ /
tadevaṃ pañcaprakārā samāsoktiḥ /
iyaṃ ca śuddhakāryasamāropeṇa viśeṣaṇasāmyenobhayamayatvena prathamaṃ tridhā samāsoktiḥ /
viśeṣaṇasāmyaṃ ca pañcaprakāraṃ nirṇītam /
sarvatra cātra vyavahārasamāropa eva jīvitam /
sa ca laukike vastuni laukikavastuvyavahārasamāropaḥ /
śāstrīye vastuni śāstrīyavastuvyavahārasamāropaḥ /
laukike vā śāstrīyavastuvyavahārasamāropaḥ /
śāstrīye vā laukikavastuvyavahāramāropa iti caturdhā bhavati /
tadevaṃ bahuprakārā samāsoktiḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, one [variety of <s>samāsokti</s>] is produced by a qualifier with <s>śleṣa</s>. That produced by a common qualifier, however, is twofold — through superimposition of an effect (<s>dharma</s>) and through superimposition of a result (<s>kārya</s>). That produced by a qualifier with simile-content is twofold — through a combination with <s>upamā</s> and through a compound [expression]. But the two varieties through a <s>rūpaka</s> combination are not within its scope. Thus <s>samāsokti</s> is of five varieties. And this <s>samāsokti</s> is first threefold — through pure superimposition of a result, through similarity of qualifier, and through being constituted of both. And the similarity of qualifier has been determined to be of five varieties. And in all cases, the life [of this figure] is the superimposition of a conventional usage (<s>vyavahāra-samāropa</s>). And this is fourfold: superimposition of a worldly convention upon a worldly thing; superimposition of a technical convention upon a technical thing; superimposition of a technical convention upon a worldly thing; and superimposition of a worldly convention upon a technical thing. Thus <s>samāsokti</s> is of many varieties.
Of these, through pure superimposition of a result, for example:

children.text: 'vilikhati kucāvuccairgāḍhaṃ karoti kacagrahaṃ likhati lalite vaktre pattrāvalīmasamañjasām /
children.translated_text: 'He scratches the breasts deeply, makes a firm hair-pulling, draws an improper pattern of leaf-designs on the lovely face,

children.text: kṣitipa khadiraḥ śroṇībimbād vikarṣati cāṃśukaṃ marubhuvi haṭhāt trasyantīnāṃ tavārimṛgīdṛśām' //
children.translated_text: and forcefully pulls the garment from the hip-region — O king, the <s>khadira</s> (acacia thorn-bush) [does all this] to the doe-eyed women of your enemies fleeing in haste through the desert!'
Here, through the superimposition of pure results — such as drawing leaf-designs — the <s>khadira</s> tree is perceived as a forceful lover. [This] was illustrated through similarity of qualifier.
Through being constituted of both, for example:

children.text: 'nirlūnānyalakāni pāṭitamuraḥ kṛtsno 'dharaḥ khaṇḍitaḥ karṇe rugjanitā kṛtaṃ ca nayane nīlābjakānte kṣatam /
children.translated_text: 'The locks are shorn, the chest is torn open, the entire lower lip is cut, a wound is made on the ear, and a gash [is inflicted] on the beautiful blue-lotus [eye].

children.text: yāntīnāmatisaṃbhramākulapadanyāsaṃ marau nīrasaiḥ kiṃ kiṃ kaṇṭakibhiḥ kṛtaṃ na tarubhistvadvairivāmabhruvām' //
children.translated_text: What has not been done by the pitiless thorn-bushes to the arch-browed wives of your enemies, as they ran through the desert with feet stumbling in extreme haste?'

children.text:
atra nīrasaiḥ kaṇṭakibhiriti viśeṣaṇasāmyam /
nirlūnānyalakānītyādiṣu kāryasamāropaḥ /
vyavahārasamāropaprakāracatuṣṭaye krameṇodāharaṇam /

children.translated_text: For example:
'It embraced the sky, quickly kissed the faces of the directions, scratched with fingertips the moonlight whose garment was restrained.

children.text: antarnimagracarapuṣpaśaro 'titāpāt kiṃ kiṃ cakāra taruṇo na yadīkṣaṇāgniḥ' //
children.translated_text: The flower-arrow of love, submerged within, from excessive heat — what did the young fire of the glance not do?'

Here, 'pitiless' and 'thorn-bearing' constitute the similarity of qualifier. 'The locks are shorn' etc. constitute the superimposition of results. [Now,] examples in order of the four varieties of superimposition of convention:
And a worldly thing can be imagined in many varieties through the distinctions of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) etc.
'By those who, seeing you as of one form in all your states, have undertaken [the task] because of your immeasurability,

children.text: lopaḥ kṛtaḥ kila paratvajuṣo vibhakte- stairlakṣaṇaṃ tava kṛtaṃ dhruvameva manye' //
children.translated_text: the elision of the case-ending denoting the attribute of superiority was surely performed — I think they [the grammarians] have created your definition!'
Here, upon a thing established in scripture (<s>āgama-śāstra</s>), there is superimposition of a convention established in grammar (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>).

children.text: 'sīmānaṃ na jagāma yannayanayornānyena yatsaṃgataṃ na spṛṣṭaṃ vacasā kadācidapi yad dṛṣṭopamānaṃ na yat /
children.translated_text: 'That which has not reached a limit to the eyes, which has not been equaled by another, which has never been touched by speech, which has no comparable standard seen,

children.text: arthādāpatitaṃ na yanna ca na yattatkiñcideṇīdṛśāṃ lāvaṇyaṃ jayati pramāṇarahitaṃ cetaścamatkārakam' //
children.translated_text: which has not arisen from any [known] meaning, and which is not nothing — such beauty of these doe-eyed ones conquers [all], beyond proof, astonishing the mind!'

children.text:
atra lāvaṇye laukike vastuni mīmāṃsāśāstraprasiddhavastusamāropaḥ /
evaṃ tarkāyurvedajyotiḥśāstraprasiddhavastusamāropo boddhavyaḥ /

children.translated_text: For example:
'Showing distinction in the cause of love, which is graceful with the charm of its own faction,
the scholarship of the cuckoo in arousing the passion of all young men was unbroken.'

Here, upon beauty — a worldly thing — there is superimposition of a convention established in <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> (scriptural hermeneutics). Similarly, superimposition of conventions from logic (<s>tarka</s>), medicine (<s>Āyurveda</s>), and astronomy (<s>Jyotiḥśāstra</s>) should be understood.
Here, there is superimposition of a convention established in the science of logic (<s>Tarkaśāstra</s>).
The word 'scholarship' (<s>pāṇḍitya</s>) is to be explained in the present context through secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>).
'Slow, unripe, sweet, of the nature of <s>Amala</s> fruit — and darkness appeared with swelling;
the eyes suffered from an affliction born of dimness — a fault, in the absence of the Lord of Herbs (the moon).'
Here, there is superimposition of a convention established in <s>Āyurveda</s> (medical science).

children.text: 'gaṇḍānte madadantināṃ prahṛrataḥ kṣmāmaṇḍale vaidhṛte rakṣāmācarataḥ sadā vidadhato lāṭeṣu yātrotsavam /
children.translated_text: 'Of him who strikes at the cheeks of maddened elephants, whose domain is the circle of the earth, who always conducts protection, who celebrates the festival of military expeditions in the <s>Lāṭa</s> [region],

children.text: pūrvāmatyajataḥ sthitiṃ śubhakarīmāsevyamānasya te vardhante vijayaśriyaḥ kimiva na śreyasvināṃ maṅgalam' //
children.translated_text: who does not abandon his former auspicious position, who is [always] resorted to — your glories of victory increase! What blessing is not [available] for the fortunate?'
Here, there is superimposition of a convention established in <s>Jyotiḥśāstra</s> (astronomy/astrology).

children.text: 'prasarpattātparyairapi sadanumānaikarasikai- rapi jñeyo no yaḥ parimitagatitvaṃ parijahṛt /
children.translated_text: 'He who cannot be known even by spreading implications (<s>tātparya</s>), nor by inference alone (<s>anumāna</s>), who has abandoned the state of being limited in scope,

children.text: apūrvavyāpāro guruvara! budhairityavasito na vācyo no lakṣyastava sahṛdayasyo guṇagaṇaḥ' //
children.translated_text: whose operation is unprecedented — thus it has been determined by the wise, O great teacher! Your collection of virtues is not expressible, not reachable by <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication), [but is perceived by] the sensitive (<s>sahṛdaya</s>).'

children.text:
atra bharatādiśāstraprasiddhavastusamāropaḥ /
tathā hyatra guṇagaṇagatatvena śṛṅgārādirasavyavahāraḥ pratīyate /
yato raso na tātparyaśaktijñeyaḥ /
nāpyanumānaviṣayaḥ /
na śabdairabhidhāvyāpāreṇa vācyīkṛtaḥ /
na lakṣaṇāgocaraḥ /
kiṃ tu vigalitavedyānataratvena parihṛtapārimityo vyañjanalakṣaṇāpūrvavyāpāraviṣayīkṛto 'nukāryānukartṛgatatvapari hāreṇa sahṛdayagata iti prasarpattātparyairityādipadai rasa eva pratīyate /
eva pratīyate /
evamanyadapi jñeyam /
children.translated_text: Here, there is superimposition of a convention established in the <s>śāstra</s> (science) of <s>Bharata</s> and others [i.e., <s>Nāṭyaśāstra</s>/poetics]. For here, the convention of <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> and other <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments) is perceived as pertaining to the collection of qualities. Because <s>rasa</s> is not knowable through the power of purport (<s>tātparya</s>); nor is it the object of inference (<s>anumāna</s>); nor has it been made expressible by the denotative function of words; nor is it within the scope of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification). Rather, with the complete dissolution of the boundary between knower and known, transcending all limits, made the object of the unprecedented function called <s>vyañjanā</s> (suggestion), abandoning the state of being in the imitated and the imitator — [it resides] in the sensitive (<s>sahṛdaya</s>). Thus by the words 'spreading implications' etc., <s>rasa</s> itself is perceived. Other [examples] should be understood similarly.

children.text: 'paśyantī trapayeva yatra tirayatyātmānamābhyantare yatra truṭyati madhyamāpi madhuradhvanyujjihāsārasāt /
children.translated_text: 'Where the Seeing speech (<s>Paśyantī</s>) conceals itself within, as if out of modesty; where even the Middle speech (<s>Madhyamā</s>) breaks off due to the desire to let the sweet <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) arise;

children.text: cāṭūccāraṇacāpalaṃ vidadhatāṃ vāk tatra bāhyā kathaṃ devyā te parayā prabho saha rahaḥkrīḍādṛḍhāliṅgane' //
children.translated_text: how then could the External speech (<s>Vaikharī</s>), which is inclined to the frivolity of uttering sweet words, [be present] — in the intimate embrace of Your play with the Supreme Goddess (<s>Parā</s>), O Lord?'

children.text:
atrāgamaprasiddhe vastuni laukikavastuvyavahārasamāropa /
laukikavastuvyavahāraśca rasādibhedād bahubheda ityuktaṃ prāk /
tatra śuddhakāryasamārope kāryasya viśeṣaṇatvamaupacārikamāśritya viśeṣaṇasāmyāditi lakṣaṇaṃ pūrvaśāstrānusāreṇa vihitaṃ yathākathañcid yojyam /
children.translated_text: Here, upon a thing established in <s>āgama</s> (scripture), there is superimposition of a worldly convention. And worldly convention is of many varieties through the distinctions of <s>rasa</s> etc. — as stated before. In the case of pure superimposition of a result, the definition 'through similarity of qualifier' — treating the result's status as qualifier as figurative — is to be somehow applied following the earlier authorities.
But here:
'Autumn, bearing upon a white cloud a rainbow resembling the mark of a fresh nail-scratch,
propitiating the blemished moon, made the heat of the sun even greater.'

children.text:
ityatrāsti tāvad raviśaśinornāyakatvapratītiḥ /
na cātra viśeṣaṇasāmyamiti sā kutastyā /
prasādayantī sakalaṅkamindumiti viśeṣaṇasāmyāccharadonāyikātvapratītau tadunuguṇyāt tayoḥ samāsoktyā nāyakatvapratītiriti cet ārdranakhakṣatābhamaindraṃ dhanurdadhānetyetadviśeṣaṇaṃ kathaṃ sāmyena nirdriṣṭam /
na caikadeśavivartinyupamoktā yatsāmarthyānnāyakatvapratītiḥ syāt /
tatkathamatra dhyavasthā /
atrocyate-ekadeśavivartinyupamā yadi pratipadaṃ noktā tat sā kena pratiṣiddhā /
sāmānyalakṣaṇadvāreṇāyātāyāstasyā atrāpi saṃbhavāt /
athātra nopamānatvena nāyakaḥ svasvarūpeṇa pratīyate apitu raviśaśinorevanāyakatvapratītiḥ /
tayoratra nāyakatvāt /
tadatrārdranakhakṣatābhamityatra sthitamapi śrutyopamānatvaṃ vastuparyālocanayā aindre dhanuṣi saṃcāraṇīyam, indracāpābhaṃ nakhakṣataṃ dadhāneti pratīteḥ, yathā 'dadhnā juhoti' ityādau dadhni saṃcaryate vidhiḥ /
evamiyamupamānuprāṇitā samāsoktireva /
iha punaḥ ityatra saraḥśriyāṃ nāyikātvapratītirna samāsoktyā, viśeṣaṇasāmyābhāvāt /
tasmānnāyikātropamānatvena pratīyate na tu saraḥśrīdharmatvena nāyikātvapratītirityekadeśavivartinyupamaivābhyupagamyā,gatyantarāsaṃbhavāt /
yaistunoktā teṣāmapyupasaṃkhyeyaiva /
yatra tu 'keśapāśālivṛndena' ityādau samāsoktāyāmupamāyāṃ samāsantariṇa viśeṣaṇasāmyaṃ yojayituṃ śakyaṃ tatraupamyagarbhaviśeṣaṇaprabhāvitā samāsoktireveti na virodhaḥ kaścit /
children.translated_text: In this passage, there is indeed the apprehension of the sun and moon as hero and heroine. But there is no similarity of qualifications here—so whence does that [apprehension] come? If one argues that through the similarity of qualifications in 'appeasing the blemished moon,' the apprehension of autumn as heroine follows, and through the congruity of that, the hero-designation of the two arises through <s>samāsokti</s> (compressed expression)—then how is the qualification 'bearing the rainbow resembling a moist nail-scratch' stated through similarity? Nor is there an <s>ekadeśavivartinī upamā</s> (partial simile) stated, by the force of which the hero-designation might follow. So how is the matter to be settled? To this we reply: if the <s>ekadeśavivartinī upamā</s> is not stated word by word, then by what is it prohibited? Since it may arrive here too through the general definition. Or rather, here the hero is not apprehended in his own form as the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison); rather, the hero-designation belongs to the sun and moon themselves, since they are the heroes here. Therefore, the qualification 'resembling a moist nail-scratch,' though positioned [in the text as applying to the rainbow], should, upon reflection on the actual thing, be transferred to <s>Indra</s>'s bow—since the apprehension is: 'the nail-scratch resembling the rainbow, which he bears.' Just as in the case of 'he offers with curds,' the injunction is transferred to the curds. Thus this is precisely a <s>samāsokti</s> animated by simile. But here, the heroine-designation of the lake's beauty is not through <s>samāsokti</s>, due to the absence of similarity of qualifications. Therefore, the heroine is apprehended here as the <s>upamāna</s>, not through the heroine-designation arising from being a property of the lake's beauty—thus <s>ekadeśavivartinī upamā</s> alone must be accepted, since no other possibility exists. For those who have not stated it, it should be additionally enumerated. However, where in [examples like] 'with a mass of hair-tresses,' etc., the similarity of qualifications in <s>samāsokti</s> can be coordinated within the compound by means of simile—there it is precisely a <s>samāsokti</s> empowered by simile-containing qualifications, and there is no contradiction.

children.text: sā ca samāroktirarthāntaranyāse kacitsamarthyagatatvena kacitsamarthakagatatvena ca bhavati /

children.translated_text: In order, as follows—
'Then, when autumn embraced the moon, the rainy season departed, its lightning-glances pacified.
Of which women does not the quality of beauty perish once their swelling breasts have fallen?'
And that <s>samāsokti</s> occurs in <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration) sometimes through the capacity [of the general statement] and sometimes through the capacitated [particular].
'What thought of women [distracts] the resolute man who desires to conquer the unconquered?

children.text: anākramya jagat sarve no saṃdhyāṃ bhajate raviḥ' //
children.translated_text: The sun does not resort to the evening twilight (<s>saṃdhyā</s>) without first having traversed the entire world.'

children.text:
atropagūḍhatvena śāntataḍitkaṭākṣatvena ca śaśāṅkaśaradornāyakavyavahārapratītau samāsoktyāliṅgita evārtho viśeṣarūpaḥ sāmānyāśrayeṇārthāntaranyāsena samarthyate /
sāmānyasya cātra śleṣavaśādutthānam /

children.translated_text: The qualification 'with pacified lightning-glances,' which contains a simile, is here in common through its basis in the compound as an intermediate [element].

children.text: asamātpetyādau tu strīśabdasya sāmānyena strītvamātrābhidhānāt sāmānyarūpo 'rtho liṅgaviśeṣanirdeśagarbheṇa kāryāpanibandhanenotthāpitayā samāsoktyā samāropitanāyakavyavahāreṇa ravisaṃdhyāvṛttāntena viśeṣarūpeṇa samarthyate /
children.translated_text: But in 'of the man who desires to conquer the unconquered,' etc., since the word 'woman' (<s>strī</s>) denotes only 'womanhood' in general, the meaning of a general nature is corroborated by the particular nature in the form of the sun-and-twilight episode, in which the hero-designation is superimposed through <s>samāsokti</s> generated by the causal connection within the designation of gender.
'As if to soothe the churning-pain of the ocean, whose serpent-king's sloughed skin-wrapping swiftly fell away under the force of the pulling,
the <s>Mandākinī</s> (celestial Gaṅgā) quickly coiled around the base of his foot.'

Here, the hero-heroine designation of the moon and autumn is apprehended through <s>samāsokti</s> by means of 'embracing' and 'pacified lightning-glances'; and the meaning, which is of a particular nature [and] embraced by <s>samāsokti</s>, is corroborated by <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> through a general statement. And here the general statement arises through the force of <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning).

children.text:
atra nirmokapaṭṭāpahnavena samāropitāyā mandākinyā yadvastuvṛttena pādamūle veṣṭanaṃ taccaraṇamūle veṣṭanatvena śleṣamūlayātiśayoktyādhyavasīyate /
tat tathādhyavasitaṃ manthavyathāvyupaśamārthamivetyutprekṣāmutthāpayati /
sotthāpyamānaivāmburāśimandākinyoḥ patipatnīvyavahārāśrayāṃ samāsoktiṃ garbhīkaroti /
evaṃ cotprekṣāsamāsoktyorekaḥ kālaḥ /
evaṃ 'nakhakṣatānīva vanasthalīnām' ityatrāpi vanasthalīnāṃ nāyikāvyavahāra utprekṣāntarānupraviṣṭasamāsoktimūla eva /
evamiyaṃ samāsoktiranantaprapañcetyanayā diśā svayamutprekṣyā /
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>Mandākinī</s>, which is superimposed [as a wife] through the concealment of the serpent-skin wrapping, has its coiling at the base of the foot as an actual event; that is determined through <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) based on <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning) as coiling at the foot of [the Lord]. That, so determined, generates the <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) 'as if to soothe the churning-pain.' That <s>utprekṣā</s>, even as it is being generated, incorporates within itself the <s>samāsokti</s> based on the husband-wife designation of the ocean and <s>Mandākinī</s>. Thus the <s>utprekṣā</s> and <s>samāsokti</s> are simultaneous. Similarly, in 'nail-scratches as if of the forest-tracts,' the hero-heroine designation of the forest-tracts is rooted in <s>samāsokti</s> which has entered within another <s>utprekṣā</s>. Thus this <s>samāsokti</s> has infinite elaboration and should be investigated in this direction by oneself.
START Sūtra 33:
The purposefulness of qualifications is <s>parikara</s> (contextual embellishment). || 33 ||
And precisely because [the qualifications] consist of lucid yet profound words, this is not the domain of <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion).

children.text: evaṃ ca pratīyamānāṃśasya vācyonmukhatvātparikara iti sārthakaṃ nāma /
children.translated_text: And thus, since the implied portion faces toward the expressible, the name '<s>parikara</s>' (attendant) is meaningful.

children.text: 'rājño mānadhanasya kārmukabhṛto duryodhanasyāgrataḥ pratyakṣaṃ kurubāndhavasya miṣataḥ karṇasya śalyasya ca /
children.translated_text: 'Before King <s>Duryodhana</s>, rich in pride, bearing a bow, in plain sight of <s>Karṇa</s>, the kinsman of the <s>Kurus</s>, and of <s>Śalya</s>, watching—

children.text: pītaṃ tasya mayādya pāṇḍavavadhūkeśāmbarākarṣiṇaḥ koṣṇaṃ jīvata eva tīkṣṇakarajakṣuṇṇādasṛgvakṣasaḥ' //
children.translated_text: today I have drunk the warm blood from the chest of that one [<s>Duḥśāsana</s>], the dragger of the hair and garments of the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> wives, while he was still alive, [the chest] crushed by my sharp nails.'
Its mention here is in the context of the discussion of the variety of qualifications. The purposefulness of qualifications means the incorporation of an implied meaning.

children.text:
atra rājña ityādau sotprāsatvaparaṃ prasannagambhīrapadatvam /
evam-
'aṅgāja senāpate rājavallabha droṇopahāsin karṇaṃ, sāṃprataṃ rakṣainaṃ bhīmād duḥśāsanam' ityādau jñeyam /
children.translated_text: Here, in 'of the king' etc., the lucid yet profound words carry the intent of derision. Similarly, in: '<s>Aṅgaja</s> (son of <s>Aṅga</s>), O commander, O favorite of the king, O scorner of <s>Droṇa</s>—O <s>Karṇa</s>, now protect this <s>Duḥśāsana</s> from <s>Bhīma</s>!'—the same principle should be understood.
START Sūtra 34:
When there is similarity of the qualified [noun] as well, and both are initially presented, [the figure is] <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning / paronomasia). || 34 ||

children.text:
kevalaviśeṣasāmyaṃ samāsoktāvuktan /
viśeṣyayuktaviśeṣaṇasāmyaṃ tvadhikṛtyedamucyate /
tatra dvayoḥ prākaraṇikayoraprākaraṇikayoḥ prākaraṇikāprakaraṇikayor vā śliṣṭapadopanibandhe śleṣaḥ /
tatrādyaṃ prakāradvayaṃ viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyasāmya eva tṛtīyastu prakāro viśeṣaṇasāmya eva bhavati /
viśeṣyasāmye tvarthaprakaraṇādinā vācyārthaniyame 'rthāntaragatadhvanerviṣayaḥ syāt /
ādye tu prakāradvaye dvayorapyarthayorvācyatvam /
ata evātra - 'dvayorvopādāne' iti tṛtīyaprakāraviṣayatvenoktam /
'viśeṣyasyāpi sāmye' iti tu śiṣṭaprakāradvayaviṣayam /
children.translated_text: The similarity of qualifications alone was discussed under <s>samāsokti</s>. But when the similarity involves the qualified [noun] together with its qualifications, this is stated. There, when there is a construction of words with double meaning involving two contextual [subjects], two non-contextual [subjects], or a contextual and a non-contextual [subject], it is <s>śleṣa</s>. Of these, the first two types involve the similarity of both qualifier and qualified, while the third type involves only the similarity of qualifications. When there is similarity of the qualified, the expressible meaning is restricted by the context of meaning etc., and [the figure] would be in the domain of <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) pertaining to another meaning. But in the first two types, both meanings are expressible. Therefore, 'when both are presented' is stated with reference to the third type. 'When there is similarity of the qualified as well' pertains to the remaining two types.
Examples in order—

children.text: 'yena dhvastamanobhavena balijitkāyaḥ purāstrīkṛto yaścodvṛttabhujaṅgahāravalayo gaṅgā ca yo 'dhārayat /
children.translated_text: 'He by whom, having destroyed <s>Manobhava</s> (the god of love), the body of the conqueror of <s>Bali</s> was formerly made into three [parts]; who bore <s>Gaṅgā</s>, whose necklaces are the coils of raised serpents, and whose glory—

children.text: yasyāhuḥ śaśimacchirohara iti stutyaṃ ca nāmāmarāḥ pāyātsa svayamandhakakṣayakarastvāṃ sarvadomādhavaḥ' //
children.translated_text: whom the immortals call by the praiseworthy name 'Bearer of the moon on the head'—may that <s>Mādhava</s>, himself the destroyer of <s>Andhaka</s>, the giver of all, protect you!'
'Dragged into confusion by greedy [hunters] with many arrows,
upon seeing that [plight], the aged ones of the forest resemble the lotuses in the pool.'

children.text: 'svecchopajātaviṣayo 'pi na yāti vaktuṃ dehīti mārgaṇaśataiśca dadāti duḥkham /
children.translated_text: 'Though his sphere of activity arises spontaneously, he does not go to say 'Give!' yet through hundreds of solicitations causes suffering;
in delusion he suddenly snatches away life itself—wretched! The god of love is like the hard-to-fathom lord (<s>Īśvara</s>).'

children.text:
atra hariharayorddhayorapi prākaraṇikatvam /
padmānāṃ mṛgāṇāṃ copamānatvādaprākaraṇikatvarm /
iśvaramanobhavayoḥ prākaraṇikāprākaraṇikatvam /
evaṃ ca śabdārthobhayagatatvena vartamānatvāttrividhaḥ /
tatrodāttādisvarabhedātprayantabhedācca śabdānyatve śabdaśleṣaḥ /
yatra prāyeṇa padabhaṅgo bhavati /
arthaśleṣastu yatra svarādibhedo nāsti /
ata eva na tatra sabhaṅgapadatvam /
saṃkalanayā tūbhayaśleṣaḥ /

children.translated_text: As follows—
'Bearing the state of having red coverings, being full-blown, not forming a connection with water,

children.text: nirasya puṣpeṣu ruciṃ samagrāṃ padmā virejuḥ śramaṇā yathaiva' //
children.translated_text: having cast off all beauty in flowers—the lotuses shone forth just like renunciant monks (<s>śramaṇas</s>).'

Here, <s>Hari</s> and <s>Hara</s> are both contextual. Lotuses and deer, being the <s>upamānas</s> (standards of comparison), are non-contextual. The lord and the god of love [represent] a contextual and a non-contextual [pair]. And thus, since [<s>śleṣa</s>] operates in word, meaning, and both combined, it is threefold. Of these, in verbal <s>śleṣa</s> (<s>śabda-śleṣa</s>), there are differences in accent such as <s>udātta</s> etc. and differences in articulation—where generally there is a breaking of words. But in <s>śleṣa</s> of meaning (<s>artha-śleṣa</s>), there is no difference of accent etc.; therefore, there is no breaking of words there. Through combination, however, there is <s>śleṣa</s> of both.

children.text:
atra raktacchadatvamityādāvarthaśleṣaḥ /
nālamityādau śabdaśleṣaḥ /
ubhayaghaṭanāyāmubhayaśleṣaḥ /
granthagauravabhayāttu pṛthaṅnodāhṛtam /
children.translated_text: Here, in 'bearing the state of having red coverings' etc. there is <s>śleṣa</s> of meaning. In 'not enough' / 'stalks' (<s>nālam</s>) etc. there is <s>śleṣa</s> of word. In the combination of both, there is <s>śleṣa</s> of both. Due to fear of prolixity, they are not illustrated separately.
